4b2a66c0d928d830: JERANTUT: A senior citizen lost RM113,550 to a phone scam last month after a caller posing as a police officer told him he was involved in money laundering.
The 69-year-old victim, who panicked after being told he was involved in the illicit activity, withdrew money from automated teller machines (ATMs) before depositing it into unknown bank accounts.
Jerantut police chief Superintendent Noor Azman Yusof said the victim received a phone call from someone posing as a policeman on Sept 11.
"The caller told the victim that he was involved in money laundering activities. The victim chose not to inform his children about the allegations.
"He withdrew a total of RM113,550 on 20 occasions via ATMs at two banks in Jerantut and Jengka between Sept 11 and yesterday before depositing the money into unknown bank accounts," he said.
Noor Azman said the victim only realised that he had been cheated after telling his children about the allegations. He lodged a police report yesterday.
He advised the public not to panic or fall for calls from unknown numbers claiming that they were involved in criminal cases or threatening them with legal action.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating.
36487f40e2571f0b: SINGAPORE, Oct 4 — Four master tenants at Punggol East Container Park and the nearby Tebing Lane will be offered a lease extension of up to one year, until the end of 2027.
This follows reports of Punggol East Container Park’s closure on November 1 for future residential redevelopment.
Punggol MP Yeo Wan Ling said yesterday that she recently met the relevant agencies to discuss concerns raised by the businesses there regarding the upcoming expiry of their tenancies.

“Following a review and adjustments to the development timelines, the agencies will be able to offer the four master tenants an extension of up to one year, until end-2027,” she wrote in a Facebook post.

“This will provide more time for them to work through their transition and business continuity plans, including engagements with their sub-tenants, subject to the relevant tenancy and regulatory requirements.
Yeo did not name the leaseholders.

Agencies including the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), JTC Corporation, National Parks Board and Housing Development Board will continue to assist affected businesses in exploring alternative premises — suitable options in the Punggol area, where available — by connecting them with the relevant government landlords and agencies, she added.
The site’s tenancy runs until December 31. After this date, the area will undergo residential development, according to SLA.

Punggol East Container Park’s master tenant City Sprouts said it received an official notice in May to vacate the site and carry out necessary reinstatement works within the stipulated timeline, The Straits Times reported.
City Sprouts added that it will offer its Punggol community farmers the opportunity to relocate to its new space at Pasir Ris Park, or other community greenhouses in the nation.

“I am glad that the agencies have been able to provide this additional flexibility. I hope the extension will give businesses more time to prepare for the transition, while allowing the community to continue enjoying these spaces as the area prepares for its next chapter,” Yeo wrote.
She also told Lianhe Zaobao that the lease extension is solely intended for affected businesses to have more time to make alternative arrangements.
The tenants must decide whether to accept the extension, comply with regulations and coordinate with subtenants and the relevant authorities, she added.
The Punggol East Container Park has been operating for around 10 years.
Isrudy Shaik, owner of halal barbecue eatery Smok Hous at the container park, posted a video on August 29 sharing news its upcoming closure.

At the time, The Smok Hous told AsiaOne that it had been informed in July of the upcoming closure by its landlord, stating that the land the container park was on will be taken back by the government. — AsiaOne
916a5566ba9c6281: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government is actively discussing the possibility of having Malaysia back on the Formula One (F1) calendar.
Speaking to Sky Sports commentator Martin Brundle during a live pre-race grid walk at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), Anwar said this was being looked into.
"Well, I'm looking forward to it. We are discussing," he said in a brief reply to Brundle.
Anwar, who was soaked after heavy rain drenched the circuit earlier, said he was nevertheless excited by the return of F1 action to Sepang.
"Oh yes. You see, I'm wet, drenched, but excited. You see, the entire country is rejoicing," he said.
Meanwhile, in a social media post, Anwar said he earlier toured the SIC's G Hillstand to meet racing fans.
He praised the lively atmosphere and the Karnival Litar Rasa Madani, which featured around 40 local traders selling meals, drinks and snacks.

"Credit also to the Cooperatives and Entrepreneur Development Cooperation, Youth and Sports Ministry as well as all agencies involved in making this carnival a success, thus ensuring that the F1's festivities also lead to benefits for our local traders," he said.
The F1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia marks the return of the sport to Sepang after a nine-year absence, with the circuit last hosting an F1 race in 2017.
The 2026 event, held from Oct 2 to 4, was relocated from Bahrain to Sepang following an agreement involving the Malaysian and Bahrain governments, F1 and the FIA.
e9a48b455bbea44c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon returned to the capital’s streets, drawing thousands of runners across multiple categories, with Kenyan athletes dominating the full marathon and Malaysian runners making their mark on home soil.
Ezekiel Kemboi led a Kenyan clean sweep of the men’s full marathon, crossing the line in 2:21:15, while Yeow Ni Jia topped the Malaysian men’s category in 2:33:52.
The results were announced by the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon on social media.
Asics Half Marathon Malaysian Men’s Veteran
Asics Half Marathon Malaysian Women’s Veteran
Among the participants, Muar MP Syed Saddiq Abdul Rahman completed the Asics Half Marathon with a personal best of 1 hour 38 minutes.
The 33-year-old politician described the run as his “last before marriage,” with his fiancée, actress and singer Bella Astillah, waiting at the finish line.
25780ea7ecff677d: KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has revised the MARCWatch status on Zetrix AI Bhd to "Negative" from "Developing", citing growing concerns over the company's transparency and governance.
The rating agency said it still lacked key information to assess the company's credit profile despite repeated requests.
This includes details on the substantial increase in borrowings and the allocation and utilisation of sizeable development expenditure, MARC Ratings said in a statement.
Its concerns were compounded by the resignation of Zetrix AI's external auditor, reported payment arrears and the suspension of certain operations.
Zetrix AI's Islamic Medium-Term Notes Programme of up to RM2 billion was rated AA-IS before the company was first placed on MARCWatch in September.
MARC Ratings said the revision to MARCWatch Negative reflected an increased likelihood of a rating downgrade.
"The MARCWatch status will remain in place pending the receipt of sufficient information and satisfactory clarification of the issues identified.
"Should the required information continue to be unavailable, or prove inadequate to support a reliable credit assessment, MARC Ratings may suspend the rating and subsequently withdraw it," it said.

f3b625581d803a5a: ISKANDAR PUTERI: A 28-year-old woman was killed when the car she were travelling in crashed into a road barrier along the Kota Iskandar highway here, today.
A 27-year-old man in the vehicle sustained minor injuries in the incident.
It is yet to be determined who was the driver.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department operation commander Saifulnizam Salleh said seven rescuers were deployed to the scene following the 10.54am distress call.
Upon arriving they found the car had veered off the highway near a new development project along Jalan Bukit Indah-Puteri Harbour before crashing into the barrier.
The woman was pronounced dead at the scene by an accompanying medical assistant, while the man was rushed to the hospital.
The operation was brought under control at 12.36pm and concluded at 12.50pm.
Police are yet to release any details.
d3a7cc44d3d2127d: KUALA LUMPUR: Transport Minister Anthony Loke will hold a press conference tomorrow morning on the Road Transport Department's (RTD) suspension of My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd as collection agents.
The press conference will take place at the Transport Ministry in Putrajaya at 11am.
On Friday, the RTD announced that the services of My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd as collection agents would be suspended effective Oct 5.
Both companies are under the MYEG Group.

The suspension followed reports that Zetrix AI owes the government more than RM200 million in unremitted collections from traffic summonses, road tax and driving licence renewals dating back to May 2023.
Yesterday, Malaysia Corruption Watch called on Putrajaya to explain how the two companies failed to remit up to RM200 million in revenue collected on behalf of the RTD.
Calling for an audit, the anti-corruption watchdog said money collected on behalf of the government must have a clear audit trail from the point of payment until the funds reach government accounts.
2a68d654e8d44a14: OCTOBER 4 — In aviation, a lie can become an operational hazard. False information can alter a pilot's decisions, mobilise rescue services and trigger security responses with consequences for human life. Fabricating a crash or staging a hijacking therefore raises a question more serious than whether a stunt is offensive: has deception crossed the threshold into unlawful endangerment?

International law provides important answers, but precision matters. A false social-media announcement is not legally identical to a fabricated threat communicated to a flight crew. An authorised emergency exercise is different from deceiving aviation authorities. The absence of deaths does not establish innocence, just as public outrage does not establish every element of an offence. — AFP pic

International law provides important answers, but precision matters. A false social-media announcement is not legally identical to a fabricated threat communicated to a flight crew. An authorised emergency exercise is different from deceiving aviation authorities. The absence of deaths does not establish innocence, just as public outrage does not establish every element of an offence.

Article 1(1)(e) of the 1971 Montreal Convention directly addresses someone who unlawfully and intentionally communicates information they know to be false, thereby endangering an aircraft in flight. A crash is not required. Knowledge of falsity and the resulting danger to the aircraft are central. [1]

The distinction matters. A fabricated bomb warning can have legal consequences even when the aircraft lands safely. Conversely, an honestly reported concern that proves unfounded is not automatically a deliberate falsehood. Passenger distress alone cannot substitute for evidence of the danger required by this provision.

Hijacking requires a separate analysis. Under the 1970 Hague Convention, the core offence involves someone aboard an aircraft in flight unlawfully seizing or exercising control through force, threats of force or intimidation. An imaginary bomb can therefore support a real hijacking if the threat achieves the unlawful seizure of control. [2]

But a performance during which the pilot retains lawful control does not automatically establish that offence merely because passengers were deceived. Other offences may still arise. The 2010 Beijing Protocol broadens the framework, including technological means and specified threats made in circumstances indicating credibility. Treaty participation and the date of the conduct determine which framework applies. [3]

False distress communications also deserve attention. Article 47 of the International Telecommunication Union Constitution requires member states to take steps to prevent false or deceptive distress, urgency, safety or identification signals. Radio Regulations provision 15.1 prohibits false or misleading transmissions. A fabricated crash report accompanied by a false distress signal may therefore engage obligations beyond the hijacking conventions. [4]

State involvement makes the stakes greater. Article 4 of the Chicago Convention commits contracting states not to use civil aviation for purposes inconsistent with the convention's aims. Sovereignty over airspace carries responsibilities; it cannot itself legitimise manufacturing a threat for political advantage. [5]

The diversion of Ryanair Flight FR4978 to Minsk on 23 May 2021 supplies a documented institutional example. ICAO Assembly Resolution A41-1 records the Council's determination that senior Belarusian government officials knowingly participated in, or were involved in, supplying information about a false bomb threat that led to the diversion. [6]

The Assembly endorsed the determination that the government's actions deliberately endangered the aircraft and those aboard, amounting to a flagrant and serious violation of Article 4. This demonstrates the international consequences of a fabricated threat without a crash. It must, however, be distinguished from a criminal conviction of any particular individual.

State responsibility and individual criminal liability are separate questions. The International Law Commission's articles on state responsibility provide a framework for asking whether conduct is attributable to a state and breaches its international obligations. State organs, delegated governmental authority, instructions and control can be relevant. Political benefit alone does not prove attribution. [7]

If an aviation incident is fabricated to blame another country and justify military action, the United Nations Charter's prohibition on the use of force also becomes relevant. Applying its principles, a state cannot manufacture a right of self-defence from an attack it knows never occurred. A false narrative cannot supply the missing factual basis. [8]

During armed conflict, international humanitarian law distinguishes permissible ruses from perfidy. Article 37 of Additional Protocol I prohibits killing, injuring or capturing an adversary through betrayal of confidence in protection afforded by that law. Not every deception meets those requirements. Calling conduct a war crime requires proof of the relevant context and elements. [9]

The practical response should combine institutional resolve with fair process. Investigators need preserved communications, crew testimony, flight data and a reconstruction of operational decisions. Alleged state involvement requires careful examination of instructions and institutional links. Authorities must establish jurisdiction and the applicable domestic implementing law, rather than assume that every treaty permits every country to prosecute every incident.

The same evidential discipline must govern accusations that a disaster was staged. Incomplete footage, early inconsistencies or unanswered questions do not themselves establish a conspiracy. Demanding a credible explanation is legitimate. Converting uncertainty into an unsupported allegation damages the very public trust that accountability is supposed to protect.

Aviation depends on people treating emergency information as a responsibility. Deliberately exploiting that trust warrants consequences where the legal elements are proved. International law earns its authority by protecting life firmly and assessing accusations fairly. The trust that allows humanity to cross the skies must never become a prop in somebody else's performance.
*This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
df5a8748fd9106eb: KANGAR, Oct 4 — Perlis police have confirmed receiving another report against a male motivational speaker over an allegation of sexual harassment.
Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the report was received yesterday and involved a 19-year-old female complainant.

“The case is being investigated under Section 509 of the Penal Code, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act,” he said in a statement today.
Hamzah said the man is currently under a two-day remand order ending today in connection with a police report lodged in Padang Besar.
He said the motivational speaker would be released on police bail before being re-arrested by Kangar police for further action.
He added that an application for remand to assist investigations into the Kangar case would be made at the Kangar Magistrates’ Court tomorrow. — Bernama
2ab6d5f4083f08cb: NAGOYA: The failure of four sports — athletics, swimming, archery and shooting — to deliver medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games has prompted a review of their planning and development systems.

National Sports Council (NSC) director-general Jefri Ngadirin said a joint assessment with the respective associations and coaching teams was needed to identify weaknesses that prevented athletes from mounting a stronger challenge at the Games.

"Athletics, archery, swimming and shooting are capable of competing at a higher level. However, we need to reassess the planning with the associations and coaches and identify the necessary measures to ensure they become more competitive," he said at a press conference on the Malaysian contingent's performance here today.
Jefri said the fact that athletes could succeed at the SEA Games but were unable to replicate that success at the Asian Games showed there was still a gap that needed to be addressed.
"They managed to win gold medals at the SEA Games, but have yet to strike gold at the Asian Games.
"So, all support, assistance and planning need to be coordinated with the associations and coaches so that the athletes can reach a higher level," he said.

Jefri said the disparity in competitive standards was also evident in swimming, with the national swimmers needing to strengthen their performances at the Southeast Asian level before setting their sights on the Asian Games podium.
"For swimming, they need to compete at the SEA Games level first before looking at opportunities to win medals at the Asian Games. They still have a long way to go.
"As for athletics, they failed this time and the coaches and association need to review the planning and address the weaknesses," he said.
Jefri said the failure in Aichi-Nagoya should not simply be viewed as a medal-less outing, but should instead lead to concrete action ahead of future Games.

"We need to have more discussions with the associations to improve the system. Planning needs to begin now, including training, association management and coaching, so that they can prepare better," he said.
Meanwhile, Olympic Council of Malaysia (OCM) secretary-general Datuk Mohd Nasir Ali said competition exposure, equipment and coaching needed specific attention, especially in archery and shooting.
"If we look at their capabilities, we actually have potential in these two sports. It is just that there is room for improvement in terms of equipment, coaches and competition exposure.
"I found that some athletes do not compete in many tournaments in a year, perhaps only two or three. So, areas such as equipment and competition exposure need to be reviewed," he said.
Nasir also stressed the importance of sound association management in ensuring athlete development was carried out systematically, especially in sports that failed to meet their targets.

"What is also important is the management of associations. For sports that have not performed as expected, we need to look at the associations' ability to manage athletes and provide strategic planning.
"Every association must have short-, medium- and long-term plans," he said.
On athletics, Nasir said more realistic targets needed to be set to help the sport regain its competitiveness on the Asian stage.
"One of the sports we should look at is athletics. We need to restore the glory of athletics.
"We are not expecting five or six medals, but at least we should be able to win one or two," he said. - Bernama

87850b40c79b048e: SEOUL, Oct 4 — Stray Kids will not be submitting their music for next year’s Grammy Awards, joining BTS in boycotting the event after the Recording Academy confirmed it would proceed with its new Asian Pop category.
JYP Entertainment, the group’s agency, told Billboard and the BBC on Friday that Stray Kids had opted out of the 69th Grammy Awards, scheduled for February 2027, Korea JoongAng Daily reported.
The announcement came after the Academy said it would present the Best Asian Pop Music Performance award as planned.

Stray Kids had been widely tipped as strong contenders, having topped the Billboard 200 album chart nine times. All eight members also hold Grammy voting rights. The BBC reported that the boycott would be a major setback for the Grammys.
The move follows BTS’s earlier decision to withdraw from the awards in protest against the new category.
735340f6f5576d84: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 4 — German rider Lennart Jasch powered his way by capturing a sensational double, winning both the overall General Classification and King of the Mountain crowns as the 2026 Le Tour de Langkawi (LTdL) concluded its eight-stage spectacle from Muar to Putrajaya, today.

The 26-year-old Tudor Pro Cycling Team rider demonstrated immense composure to defend the Orange Jersey from Stage Two where he conquered the brutal road of Gunung Jerai from Taiping, all the way to the finish line, clocking an aggregate winning time of 28 hours, 57 minutes and 02 seconds.
“Super happy. Well, it’s another really tough day, so like I said yesterday, might look easy on paper, but it was definitely (not) easy, especially the last kilometres.

“So, yeah, it was a super hard day, so I’m really thankful of the team, of all the support they gave me all week, and, yeah, I think we can all be super super proud of the performance we did this week,” he said when met after the race, today.

He finished with a comfortable 26 second cushion over his closest challenger, Abel Balderstone Roumens of Caja Rural Seguros RGA while Balderstone’s teammate Jan Castellon Ribalt rounded off the podium in third spot, 42 seconds adrift.

Adding gloss to his triumphant week, Lennart also wrapped up the tour as the undisputed King of the Mountains, winning the Polka Dot Jersey with 45 points to edge Wheeltop Rotor Chengdu Cycling Team’s Petr Rikunov (41 points) and Castellon (26 points).
Reflecting on his maiden ProSeries GC title as a neo pro, Lennart admitted that going all the way to top the podium far exceeded their pre-race target of merely chasing a top five finish.

“Yeah, extremely meaningful. I mean it’s the first pro GC I’m allowed to win, and also the first time I win a race outside of Italy. So of course the first time out of Europe also. It’s something super, super special and it will for sure stay in my mind the rest of my life.

“For sure it changes a lot at least for me, because now I know that I can be a good GC rider. I mean, I hoped for this before but I needed to prove it and now I made a first step into this direction,” he added.

Meanwhile, the final 188.3-kilometre Stage Eight was claimed by Italian, Matteo Malucelli of XDS Astana Team who clocked 4:05:17s in a bunch sprint finish to pip Riley Pickrell (Modern Adventure Pro Cycling) and Christiaan Van Rees (Team Picnic PostNL).
Malucelli’s stage triumph also cemented his grip on Blue Jersey as the Best Sprinter with 64 points ahead of Pickrell (57 points) and Nil Gimeno Ferrer of Equipo Kern Pharma (22 points).
In the Best Asian Rider category, Japan’s Yuhi Todome of Aisan Racing Team claimed the White Jersey after posting an overall time of 29:04:23s.

Meanwhile, Tsen Ren Bao of St George Continental Cycling Team emerged as the best Malaysian rider, finishing 25th in the overall General Classification (+11:05s) and taking second place in the Asian rider standings. — Bernama
68e2c2ceb472d0c4: KUALA LUMPUR: Immigration officers detained 52 foreigners in late-night raids on seven entertainment outlets in the Dang Wangi area.

The Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department said the operation, dubbed Op Gegar, began at 1.30am and involved 74 of its enforcement officers, supported by 18 from the department's Special Tactical Force (Pastak).
The raids were carried out following intelligence gathering and public tip-offs about the presence of foreigners suspected of working illegally and abusing their visit passes.
In a post on its official Facebook page, the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department said 170 people were screened during the operation.
"Of these, 52 foreigners, comprising 23 men and 29 women, were detained for various suspected immigration offences.
"The department also issued five Form 29 notices, or summonses to witnesses, to representatives of the premises to assist investigations," it said.
It added that the detainees are being investigated for various offences under the Immigration Act 1959/63, Passport Act 1966 and Immigration Regulations 1963.
"Among the suspected offences were not possessing valid travel documents, overstaying and violating the conditions of their passes.
"All detainees were taken to the Bukit Jalil Immigration depot for documentation and further investigation," it said.
Kuala Lumpur Immigration director Datuk Hamsha Injau said the enforcement operations would be intensified to ensure compliance with the country's immigration laws.
c9bda2859c2afd1c: NEW DELHI: Indian police launched an investigation on Sunday into allegations of sexual harassment against officers during protests in the capital against the country's election commission.

Protests began on Friday demanding the Election Commission of India (ECI) chief Gyanesh Kumar step down, alleging wrongdoing during a large-scale voter-roll revision that has struck millions of names from the lists.
The ECI has rejected allegations of wrongdoing. Kumar himself has not commented.
The harassment allegations were made on Saturday when police detained scores of protestors around the government-designated protest site of Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.
"Allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers," Delhi police said in a statement, promising "a fair and impartial enquiry."
In a video posted on social media, a complainant said that a police officer pushed and touched her "inappropriately."

A third day of protests is slated in the capital on Sunday, including by left-wing groups and supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) – which began in May as a satirical online movement, succeeding in its campaign to oust the then education minister.
CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke, who warned against a police crackdown and detentions on Saturday, said that the accused officer "must be arrested immediately."
Neha Bora, an activist from a left-wing student organisation, called for protesters to march to New Delhi's central India Gate.
"From Streets to Protests, Women Are NOT SAFE!," she said in a post on social media.
Opposition politicians have accused the ECI of acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
They have said they will march to the Election Commission in New Delhi on Tuesday, and hold "Save Democracy" rallies countrywide afterwards.
The CJP has called for a "massive mobilisation of young Indians" in New Delhi on Oct 10.
6dec0d8c60ae3ce0: IPOH, Oct 4 — An elderly man was killed and a woman who was the pillion rider was seriously injured after the motorcycle they were riding skidded at Lorong Kampung Boyan 1, Kampung Boyan near Taiping, today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department Assistant Director of Operations Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the 76-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene by Ministry of Health (MOH) medical officers.
He said they received a call about the incident at 12.41 pm before a fire engine from the Taiping Fire and Rescue Station arrived six minutes later.

“Upon arriving at the scene, personnel found that the Yamaha Ego motorcycle ridden by the two victims had skidded and nearly fallen into a drain in front of a house. The elderly man was unconscious while the 69-year-old woman suffered serious head injuries,” he said in a statement today.
Sabarodzi said firefighters lifted the male victim, who was nearly falling into the drain, before MOH medical officers confirmed his death.

“The injured victim was given initial treatment before being sent to the hospital, while the male victim’s body was handed over to the police for further action, and the operation ended at 1.49 pm,” he said. — Bernama
29721465c59c0a43: Unison refuses to ballot members on offer that would see thousands of council employees worse off Thousands of Glasgow council workers face being sacked and reappointed under less favourable terms in one of the UK’s biggest ever “fire-and-rehire” exercises, after union negotiations broke down once again this week. Those negotiations concerned a new pay and grading system designed to resolve historical pay equality issues. 2dae75fa19340263: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — A total of eight locations recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the unhealthy category as of 4pm today.

According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, five areas in Johor were affected, involving Segamat (156), Batu Pahat (155), Kluang (152), Tangkak (151) and Larkin (111).
In Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas were Nilai (151) and Seremban (146), while Samarahan, Sarawak, recorded a reading of 117.
Meanwhile, 57 areas were in the moderate category, while three areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and an API exceeding 300 hazardous. — Bernama
aa9d5c986b60cf27: PUTRAJAYA: Missing out on the white jersey at Le Tour de Langkawi (LTdL) has fuelled Tsen Ren Bao's determination to return and win the Asian rider classification next year.
The St George Continental Cycling Team rider finished 25th overall in the race's 30th edition, with several encouraging performances along the way.
He was the first Malaysian across the line on Stage Four from Meru Raya to Cameron Highlands on Wednesday.
Ren Bao then finished 30th on Stage Five from Tapah to Genting Highlands, one place behind his younger brother, national team rider Tsen Ren Han.
In the Asian rider classification, Ren Bao finished second, 3 minutes and 44 seconds behind Aisan Racing Team's Yuhi Todome, who clocked an overall time of 29 hours, four minutes and 23 seconds.
Terengganu Cycling Team's Kee Zhe Yie took third in 29:10:21 after overtaking Ren Han in the standings during today's final stage from Muar to Putrajaya.
"I feel relieved now, but I am still proud to have finished second.
"I did not get the jersey this year. Perhaps next year I will return with the aim of winning it," said the 23-year-old.
This year's race was also a memorable family occasion for Ren Bao, whose sister came to support him after three years apart.
His father, Tsen Seong Hoong, was also present, while Ren Han competed alongside him.
"I do not know what happened to my brother today. He lost third place in the standings, and that is something he needs to learn from.
"The difference between us is experience. I have competed in LTdL three times and raced in many other events.
"I know what to do, when to do it and how to avoid dangerous moves. That helped me get through this year's LTdL," he said.
151d628325e12ada: SINGAPORE, Oct 4 — A 42-year-old man was apprehended after he was rescued from the aircon ledge of a flat in Bukit Panjang this morning.

The police and Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) told AsiaOne they received a call for assistance at Block 635B Senja Road, where a man was spotted standing on the air-con ledge of an eighth-floor unit.
Two photographs seen by AsiaOne show at least one fire engine, a rescue tender and at least three police cars parked along a driveway near the block.
SCDF deployed a safety life air pack as a precautionary measure when they arrived at the scene.
As the man was assessed to possibly pose a danger to himself, the police activated officers from their Crisis Negotiation Unit, while SCDF deployed its Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART).
DART rescuers rappelled down from the unit above and brought the man to safety at about 9.50am.
The 42-year-old was taken conscious to hospital and subsequently apprehended under Section 7(1) of the Mental Health (Care and Treatment) Act.
Under the Act, the police have the power to arrest anyone believed to be a danger to himself or other people. — AsiaOne
da97961608ba62be: SEPANG, Oct 4 — The return of Formula 1 to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence received special attention today when His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race, together with the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei.

a7252e75a9e1d91a: FISHERMEN along Latin America's Pacific coast are reeling in half-empty nets as ocean warming aggravated by El Nino causes tuna, anchovies and other top catches to migrate to cooler waters.

From Ecuador and Peru in South America, to Panama and Guatemala in Central America, some skippers have stopped going out altogether as fish stocks dwindle close to shore, in seas running at up to six degrees Celsius above normal.
"The water is warm," Juan Ollague, 56, told AFP in the southwestern Ecuadoran port of Santa Rosa where hundreds of idle fishing boats are crammed into a small port.
After a night on the water, Ollague returns with just six small tuna.
"We came away empty-handed," he lamented.
"Fishing used to be good, now it's terrible," fellow skipper Darwin Zambrano, 53, complained as he untangled a net that hasn't scooped up big tuna like albacore or bonito in weeks.
El Nino is the warming phase of a natural cycle in the tropical Pacific that causes hotter and drier conditions in some places, and cooler and wetter in others.
This year's "super" El Nino, which is expected to peak later this year, is already wreaking havoc in Central America, where drought is endangering animals and stunting crops.

The average sea surface temperature, excluding polar regions, reached 21.07C in August, tying with March 2024 as the hottest on record, according to the European Union's Copernicus climage change observatory.

The average sea temperatures off Ecuador's coast rose by 2.5-3C at the surface and up to 6C at a depth of 40 metres in the past 10 weeks, said oceanographer Jonathan Cedeno, who led a mission from Guayaquil's Polytechnic University to measure the temperatures.
On Panama's Pacific coast, Rigoberto Gonzalez said he has to sail further and further from shore to earn a living.
This means spending more on food, ice to preserve the fish, and fuel for the small boat he uses to catch snapper, kingfish and barracuda.
"We go out with US$100 worth of gas, and when we come back, we earn US$150" from sales of the fish, which has to be divided among four workers, Gonzalez, 59, told AFP, on Veracruz beach.
In nearby Panama City, some fishermen have thrown in the towel and decided to remain in port.
"We can't keep losing money," Jesus Morales, leader of the artisanal fishermen's union of Panama, said.

Further north, in Iztapa, Guatemala, 50-year-old Eliseo Ovando said it now takes three days to catch what he used to pull from the water in a day, and complains that only commercial fisheries receive government assistance to ride out the shortages.
"The big fish eat the little ones," he said, referring to the struggles of small-scale operators like himself.
In Peru, the world's biggest catcher of anchovies, fishermen are turning to construction to feed their families as their tiny prey slips out of reach.
In Panama City, the poor yields are visible at a wholesale fish market next to the dock that supplies the city's supermarkets.
"Less is arriving" off the boats, says Carlos Nieto, a 46-year-old vendor. And sometimes the catch is "damaged by the heat," he said.
Nieto now spends about $600 a month on ice, "practically a whole salary."
For now, vendors in Panama haven't passed on their higher costs and reduced income to consumers in the form of significantly higher prices.
But in Ecuador, the world's second-largest tuna producer after Thailand, the prices of mahi-mahi (also known as dorado) and swordfish have doubled due to the shortage, according to the industry.
In Santa Rosa, the sea's dwindling bounty has a knock-on effect, leading to the temporary closure of food stalls along the port.
Francisco Orlando, who earns a living filleting fish, is worried that he could soon be out of a job.
"We're hoping they (fishermen) catch fish," the 37-year-old explained as he sharpened his knives to separate the bones from the meat.
"If they do, we work. If they don't, we don't."
* The writer is from AFP

d187fd51548671e2: TEHRAN, Oct 4 — Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said today that there was no military solution to his country’s conflict with the United States, with talks on ending the war apparently at an impasse.

A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure.

“If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force,” Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.
“There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions,” he continued, adding “only negotiations based on justice and fairness” could end the conflict.
The two sides agreed a memorandum of understanding in June aimed at providing a framework for a permanent resolution, but the deal collapsed, largely due to disagreements over the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran has sought to impose control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, and has attacked vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation.
Iranian and US officials last week held indirect talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for reopening the strait.
Trump, however, rejected the proposal, while leaving the door open both to further talks or renewed military operations.
The United States has not struck Iran since September 1.

US media outlet Axios reported that top Trump cabinet members met Friday to discuss the war in Iran, as well as the conflict in Yemen, where the Tehran-backed Houthis have been fighting government forces and attacking Saudi Arabia. — AFP
6443a96b6c130ff9: TOKYO: Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi registered a protest with the US on Sunday after a US Marine was arrested on suspicion of robbing and murdering a Japanese woman in Okinawa.

"The occurrence of such an extremely brutal and vicious incident is extremely regrettable," Takaichi said in a statement.

"The government of Japan strongly protests to the US side and strongly seeks maximum cooperation with the investigation," as well as the tightening of discipline and thorough measures to prevent a recurrence, she said.
Defence minister Shinjiro Koizumi, in comments carried by national broadcaster NHK, said: "Such an incident is unacceptable and I am deeply outraged".
The US embassy and the Marine Corps expressed condolences over the incident and said they were cooperating with the Japanese authorities.
The Marines said in a statement that the suspect, who is assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force and based at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, was in Japanese custody.
"The Marine Corps takes these allegations very seriously and expects every Marine to adhere to the highest standards of behaviour," it said.
Most of the 18,000 Japan-based Marines are stationed in Okinawa, which the US held from the end of World War Two until 1972.
Their presence has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of personnel.
The 1995 rape of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US servicemen sparked mass protests.

Saturday's killing could complicate Takaichi's efforts to relocate some ⁠Marines from the busy Futenma air base to a more remote facility at ​Henoko. Opponents want the troops moved out of the prefecture.
Okinawa, which is 100km from Taiwan at the closest point, is viewed by Tokyo and Washington as key in deterring potential military aggression from China.

4e75d3bdebaef62f: PETALING JAYA: The government is discussing the possibility of bringing back the Malaysian Grand Prix Formula One race following the return of F1 action to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) this weekend, says Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
Asked today if there was a chance Malaysia could get an F1 race back in the future, the prime minister said: “Well, I’m looking forward to it. We’re discussing.”
He was responding to former F1 driver and Sky Sports commentator Martin Brundle during a brief exchange on the grid before the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix today.
Anwar, who was drenched by the heavy rain at Sepang, also spoke of his excitement at seeing F1 back in the country.
“You see, I’m wet, drenched, but am very excited. You see, the entire country is rejoicing,” he told Brundle.
Heavy rain and standing water delayed the start of the race, with the starting procedure later suspended after the drivers went out behind the safety car, just before 4pm.
The race eventually flagged off at 4.35pm.
This weekend marks the first time a F1 race has been held at Sepang since 2017, although the event is officially known as the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
The Bahrain race was moved to SIC following security concerns arising from the conflict in the Middle East, giving Malaysia an unexpected return to the F1 calendar.

Malaysia previously hosted its own F1 race at SIC every year from 1999 to 2017. Former prime minister Najib Razak's administration ended the event after citing its high hosting costs and declining returns.

The government had said before this weekend's event that Malaysia would only need to spend between RM10 million and RM16 million on preparations, as Bahrain had already borne the major costs associated with hosting the race.
However, SIC CEO Azhan Shafriman Hanif previously estimated that securing a permanent place on the F1 calendar would cost Malaysia at least RM300 million a year, including hosting rights fees.
He said any permanent return would also depend on whether the government could justify the expenditure and whether a slot was available on the increasingly crowded F1 calendar.

6a1bb94389a2d3d1: KYIV: Russia struck a bridge in Kyiv on Sunday soon after Germany's chancellor arrived in Ukraine's capital on a surprise visit to demonstrate European support in the face of an upsurge in attacks.
Air raid sirens blared across Kyiv, urging residents to shelter, soon after Friedrich Merz's arrival under tight security, with warnings of approaching Russian attack drones.

Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko then confirmed that a strike had damaged the road surface on the Northern Bridge – one of several connecting the eastern and western parts of the city over the Dnipro river which have been struck in recent days.
Images posted on messaging channels appeared to show a missile slamming into the structure, sending a fireball into the air.
Klitschko has said that Kyiv – largely spared from the devastation wrought near the frontlines in nearly five years of conflict – should now be on a war footing due to the upsurge in attacks.
A spate of round-the-clock attacks has hit residential areas, petrol stations, schools, rail and communications infrastructure.
Merz said the country "needs all our support in the coming weeks."
"If Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us," he added.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has repeatedly urged Ukraine's Western allies for more military support, including advanced interceptors to shoot down Russia's new fast-moving, jet-powered drones.
Merz and Zelenskyy were due to meet and government sources in Berlin said they were expected to agree a new package of military support worth more than $1 billion.
It includes combat drones and satellite technology to help Ukraine hit Russian launch sites, as well as for the joint production of anti-jet drones, the German sources said.
"This support addresses the most significant current gap in Ukraine's air defence system. The impact is expected to be rapid and tangible," a source said.
Merz this week called for unity against Russia within Nato and the European Union as well as his own country, where the far-right, Moscow-friendly AfD opposition is on the rise.
There have been increasing fears in Europe that it could find itself in Russia's crosshairs, including from covert attacks, if it is not stopped in Ukraine.
On Saturday, Russia warned foreigners and diplomats to leave Kyiv, saying "massive" new airstrikes would hit the city.
The Russian foreign ministry declared in a statement that "responsibility for any potential negative consequences rests entirely with those who ignore this warning."
Moscow had issued a similar warning in May, but leaders from countries supporting Ukraine have defied the Russian warnings and continued to make visits.
"The EU Delegation is staying. Threatening us will not stop Europe's support for Ukraine. It only reminds us why that support matters!" EU ambassador Katarina Mathernova wrote on X on Sunday.
Mathernova told AFP separately that "nobody is moving", although European embassies always had contingency plans, including for winter, she added.
Russia has admitted deliberately targeting Ukraine's energy sector as winter approaches. Last year, similar attacks knocked out power and heating for days on end as temperatures plummeted to -20C.
In Kyiv, which is home to some three million people, residents have begun mulling what to do if that happens again.
The government has also suggested that the vulnerable and disabled should consider leaving.
Merz's trip was expected to announce some 350 million euros to help provide generators, transformer stations and for grid repairs, German government sources said.

5d7a5c93c758b40f: Pada pandangan saya, Malaysia tidak lagi boleh melihat kecurian kabel sebagai sekadar jenayah harta benda. Apa yang berlaku hari ini jauh lebih membimbangkan. Kegiatan ini semakin berleluasa, semakin berani dan semakin memberi kesan kepada kehidupan rakyat serta pembangunan negara.

Setiap kali saya membaca laporan mengenai kabel yang dicuri atau melihat video tular berkaitan kegiatan tersebut, persoalan yang timbul ialah sejauh mana kita benar-benar melindungi aset strategik negara. Kabel bukan sekadar logam yang boleh dijual untuk mendapatkan keuntungan. Ia merupakan nadi kepada bekalan elektrik, telekomunikasi, sistem pengangkutan dan pelbagai kemudahan awam yang digunakan setiap hari oleh jutaan rakyat.

Apa yang lebih mengecewakan ialah rakyat akhirnya menjadi mangsa. Apabila berlaku gangguan bekalan elektrik, talian komunikasi terputus atau sistem pengangkutan tergendala akibat kecurian kabel, rakyat kehilangan masa, peniaga mengalami kerugian dan kerajaan pula terpaksa mengeluarkan jutaan ringgit lagi daripada wang pembayar cukai untuk membaiki kerosakan yang sebenarnya boleh dielakkan.

Saya juga melihat kebelakangan ini terdapat kejadian yang menimbulkan kebimbangan masyarakat mengenai keberkesanan penguatkuasaan. Video-video yang tular di media sosial telah mencetuskan pelbagai persoalan dalam kalangan rakyat. Walaupun setiap insiden perlu disiasat berdasarkan fakta dan prosedur undang-undang, persepsi awam terhadap tahap penguatkuasaan tidak boleh dipandang ringan. Kepercayaan rakyat terhadap institusi penguat kuasa perlu sentiasa dipelihara melalui tindakan yang profesional, pantas dan telus.

Pada hemat saya, kesan daripada kecurian kabel jauh lebih besar daripada nilai kabel yang dicuri. Ia boleh melumpuhkan operasi perniagaan, mengganggu perkhidmatan kesihatan, menjejaskan komunikasi, mengganggu operasi industri dan memberi kesan kepada keyakinan pelabur terhadap keupayaan negara melindungi infrastruktur.

Walaupun saya tidak mengatakan bahawa setiap pelaku mempunyai motif untuk mensabotaj negara, saya berpendapat kesan yang ditinggalkan oleh kegiatan ini adalah seumpama satu bentuk sabotaj terhadap aset strategik negara. Infrastruktur yang dibina menggunakan wang rakyat telah dirosakkan demi keuntungan segelintir pihak. Akibatnya bukan sahaja ditanggung oleh kerajaan, tetapi oleh seluruh rakyat.

Bagi saya, tindakan terhadap pencuri kabel sahaja tidak mencukupi. Kerajaan perlu membongkar keseluruhan rangkaian sindiket, termasuk dalang, orang tengah, pengangkut serta mana-mana pihak yang membeli kabel atau logam yang disyaki diperoleh melalui kegiatan jenayah. Selagi ada pasaran untuk kabel curi, selagi itulah sindiket ini akan terus hidup.

Saya juga berpendapat hukuman terhadap kesalahan yang melibatkan infrastruktur kritikal negara perlu dikaji semula supaya setimpal dengan kesan yang ditanggung oleh rakyat. Pada masa yang sama, penggunaan teknologi seperti kamera pintar, dron pemantauan, sistem pengesanan kabel dan rondaan berkala perlu dipertingkatkan bagi mengurangkan peluang jenayah ini berlaku.

Bagi saya, dalam mana-mana negara, sesiapa yang sengaja merosakkan infrastruktur kritikal demi keuntungan peribadi tidak boleh lagi dianggap sekadar pencuri biasa. Mereka sedang menyerang kepentingan awam. Walaupun motifnya mungkin jenayah terancang dan bukannya operasi perisikan, kesan yang ditinggalkan adalah seumpama satu tindakan sabotaj terhadap aset strategik negara yang melemahkan keselamatan, ekonomi dan kesejahteraan rakyat.

Malaysia memerlukan pendirian yang lebih tegas dalam melindungi aset strategik. Jika kita benar-benar menghargai wang rakyat dan mahu membina sebuah negara yang maju serta berdaya saing, maka kita tidak boleh lagi berkompromi dengan jenayah yang mengancam infrastruktur negara. Pada pandangan saya, melindungi aset negara adalah tanggungjawab bersama, dan sudah tiba masanya kita menganggap kecurian kabel sebagai satu ancaman serius yang memerlukan tindakan luar biasa.
Iskandar Khoo Kuan Yiaw adalah pembaca FMT.

6f471ddbd94477ee: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — October has got off to a positive start for Malaysia, marked by a vibrant sporting calendar, strong performances by national athletes and encouraging developments in the economy and investment, while several major national agendas await as the month unfolds.

The first weekend of the month saw Malaysia become a focal point for sports fans as the roar of Formula 1 (F1) machinery once again echoed at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after nine years, with Malaysia hosting the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026.

The return of the prestigious race to Sepang, which last hosted an F1 event in 2017, coincided with two other major international sporting events, the Le Tour de Langkawi (LTdL) 2026 and the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026.

The 30th edition of LTdL, which began on Sept 27, will conclude in Putrajaya today after eight stages across the peninsula, while KLSCM, held yesterday and today, saw more than 30,000 local and international participants take to the streets of the capital.

The sporting excitement at home was accompanied by strong performances by the national contingent at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games in Japan, which had secured nine gold, seven silver and 16 bronze medals as of yesterday.

The haul included historic team gold medals for the men’s and women’s squash teams, a keirin gold for track cycling champion Datuk Mohd Azizulhasni Awang, and the men’s sepak takraw squad’s first team regu gold in 36 years.
National sporting success also extended to the football pitch as Harimau Malaya ended their Fifa Asean Cup 2026 group-stage campaign with a 6-0 victory over Singapore.
Although the result was not enough to send the national squad into the final, the team is set to face Vietnam in the third-place playoff tomorrow.

The positive trend was also reflected in the economy, with the ringgit showing resilience in a challenging global environment, ending the first week of October trading at 4.0820/4.0870 against the US dollar.
Malaysia’s investment momentum also received a boost as the country and Singapore explored efforts to attract third-country investors to the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).

Companies from the republic have so far committed more than S$5.5 billion in investments in the zone, covering sectors including advanced manufacturing, data centres, energy technology and solar energy.

On the international front, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia’s involvement was also expanding through Petronas, which holds a 25 per cent stake in the C$33 billion (about RM94.7 billion) LNG Canada Phase 2 expansion project.
The project could open up further investment and business opportunities for Malaysian companies in Canada’s energy and infrastructure sectors.

Following Anwar’s meeting with Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister, Prince Salman Hamad Al Khalifa, yesterday, Malaysia also welcomed Bahraini investments in areas including Islamic finance, technology, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and smart manufacturing.
The two countries also encouraged Malaysian companies to use Bahrain as a gateway to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) market.
Despite the positive developments at the start of October, Malaysia continues to grapple with transboundary haze, which has caused a decline in air quality in many areas nationwide.
Six areas recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels, while 37 were at moderate levels and only three recorded good readings.
As October progresses, attention will turn to several major agendas expected to shape the country’s economic and political landscape for the remainder of the year.
Most immediately, focus will be on the Dewan Rakyat sitting, which begins tomorrow, with the tabling of Budget 2027 by the Prime Minister, who is also Finance Minister, scheduled for Friday.

The budget will be among the country’s most closely watched economic agendas this year, with attention expected on measures to tackle the cost of living, raise incomes, stimulate growth and strengthen economic resilience amid a challenging global environment.

The Pre-Budget 2027 Statement had outlined 10 focus areas centred on the Madani Economy and 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) priorities, including tackling the cost of living, increasing incomes, creating quality jobs and strengthening the economy and governance.
Political activity is also expected to intensify this month as the 16th Melaka State Election (PRN) moves into the next phase following the dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly on Sept 23.

The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting this Wednesday to determine key dates for the election, including nomination and polling days, as negotiations and cooperation among political parties remain a focal point.

Senior Lecturer in Political Science at the Faculty of Administrative Science and Policy Studies, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), Mujibu Abd Muis, described October as a crucial month that could determine the direction and pace of the country’s politics in the final months of 2026.

He said developments taking place almost simultaneously, including the Melaka state election, internal party dynamics and the tabling of Budget 2027, could shape public perceptions ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16).

Mujibu viewed the Melaka state election not merely as a battleground to determine the state government, but as a potential ‘political laboratory’ for parties to test their respective strengths, strategies and cooperation formulas.

He said the election would follow two previous state polls involving Johor and Negeri Sembilan, while also providing political data that could influence seat negotiations, candidate selection and coalition alignments ahead of GE16.

Mujibu said Budget 2027 would serve as the most tangible test of the government’s economic credibility, noting that the public would evaluate it not merely based on figures but on the extent to which announced measures affect their lives, including disposable income, the cost of living, employment and economic opportunities.

“With two months remaining until the end of 2026, October provides an opportunity to assess the political landscape. Parties will look at the Melaka state election results, gauge the public’s response to the Budget, assess their respective organisational strengths and then begin making more serious calculations for GE16.

“In summary, October may not be the month that determines who will win the general election, but it could be the month that determines who starts to emerge as being in the lead, who is losing momentum and who needs to change their strategy,” he said. — Bernama
