3fd3482faa7cf322: NAGOYA, Oct 4 — The Asian Games in Japan will close later today after a fortnight of record-smashing displays from young stars, but marred by mix-ups, patchy crowds and accusations of mismanagement.
More than 17,000 athletes and officials, a bigger number than the Olympics, descended on Nagoya and Aichi prefecture for the continent’s premier sporting spectacular.
Chinese swimming sensation Yu Zidi, just 13, stole the show in the pool with three gold medals, all in Games-record times.
She looks set to be a major medal threat at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.
The schoolgirl was named a Games MVP on Sunday to cap an extraordinary showing that saw her scorch to gold in the 200m butterfly and do the 200m-400m individual medley double.
But for that all that, the shy teenager said: “I don’t think I am what people describe as a prodigy.”
Also in the pool, Japanese swimmer Shin Ohashi, himself only 17, smashed the men’s 200m breaststroke world record to delight the home crowd.
In athletics, where rain tumbled down over several days, Thai sprinter Puripol Boonson did the 100m-200m double and was named men’s MVP.
“This time there were a lot of global athletes at this event, so the MVP gives me a lot of confidence that I can make the podium in LA,” the 20-year-old said.
‘Failure grade’
With the hours ticking down to the closing ceremony, when Japan will hand over the baton to Doha, top officials were on the defensive.
Olympic Council of Asia director general Husain Al-Musallam said “numbers are facts”, pointing to 50 world records broken at the Games since they opened on September 19.
“The athletes cannot perform if they don’t sleep good, the athletes cannot perform if they don’t have good transportation,” he said.
This 20th edition of the Games, which were first contested in 1951, did not have a traditional athletes’ village in a bid to save money.
Instead, participants were housed in wooden temporary units, on a cruise ship and in hotels.
Organisers said this was a template for future multi-sports events.
But it came with issues, with some teams complaining the units were too cramped and the beds too short.
More than that, the ballooning numbers of athletes and officials meant there were not enough beds for everyone.
One Thai Olympic official told AFP it was “like musical chairs”.
The sport, including a blockbuster cricket final won by India against arch-rivals Pakistan, did sometimes shine through.
North Korean weightlifter Ri Song Gum, a 140cm pocket powerhouse, set three new world marks in one day for gold.
But problems kept coming too, including organisers playing North Korea’s national anthem for the South Korean hockey team.
There were athletes’ buses that did not turn up when they should, or did not arrive at all.
Two teams were sent to the wrong venue, delaying a volleyball match.
“If I were to give them a grade, it would be an F,” Ryu Seung-min, president of the Korean Sport and Olympic Committee, said.
Games organisers were on the back foot as well over attendances, with the opening ceremony taking place in front of thousands of empty seats.
At the women’s football semi-final between hosts Japan and South Korea there were 998 spectators in a 50,000 stadium.
Boy history-maker
Japanese Olympic Committee president Seiko Hashimoto admitted that “there were many problems”, but said the country wants to host more international events in future.
She said bad weather had turned some spectators off, but was eager to point out that some sports were well attended.
About 30,000 saw South Korea beat Japan 1-0 to clinch men’s football gold, although the occasion was tarnished somewhat when the South Korean flag failed to go up in the victory ceremony.
The hosts finished with 83 golds, a distant second in the medals table behind China with 169.
Japan’s tally included gold for Yuki Kurihara, who won an eSports competition aged 11, believed to make him the youngest Games champion in history.
Several sports with ambitions of making the Olympics made their debut, including padel, MMA and virtual taekwondo. — AFP
d8ba7e088dc1dd31: TEHERAN: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday that there was no military solution to his country's conflict with the United States, with talks on ending the war apparently at an impasse.

A campaign of heavy bombardment failed to bring a decisive close to the war launched by the US and Israel in late February, and Washington in recent weeks has dialled back military operations in favour of economic pressure.

"If our enemies again choose the path of military confrontation, our response will be stronger than before, and we will defend ourselves with even more force," Araghchi said at a gathering of foreign ambassadors.
"There is no military solution, nor any solution based on new sanctions," he continued, adding "only negotiations based on justice and fairness" could end the conflict.
The two sides agreed a memorandum of understanding in June aimed at providing a framework for a permanent resolution, but the deal collapsed, largely due to disagreements over the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran has sought to impose control over the vital shipping lane since the start of the war, and has attacked vessels that attempt to transit without its authorisation.
Iranian and US officials last week held indirect talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with Tehran saying it presented seven conditions for reopening the strait.
Trump, however, rejected the proposal, while leaving the door open both to further talks or renewed military operations.
The United States has not struck Iran since Sept 1.

US media outlet Axios reported that top Trump cabinet members met Friday to discuss the war in Iran, as well as the conflict in Yemen, where the Teheran-backed Houthis have been fighting government forces and attacking Saudi Arabia.
4485914479df1a4c: MOTEGI: Defending world champion Marc Marquez won the Japanese MotoGP on Sunday to slice Jorge Martin's overall championship lead to two points with six events of the season remaining.
Marquez pushed pole-sitter Martin into second place in Motegi after overtaking his fellow Spaniard midway through the race.
It put seven-time world champion Marquez back within touching distance of the championship lead after losing ground in the previous race in Austria.
Marquez completed the double after also winning Saturday's sprint race in Japan.
He said it was "very important" to claim maximum points from the weekend.
"The race was tough, especially when I was behind Jorge, but I knew that if I was able to lead the race the pace was good," he said.
"Jorge tried to attack but then I just increased the pace and it was enough to do the last two laps more relaxed," he added.
Italian Marco Bezzecchi finished third and slipped further behind in the title race.
Marquez dropped to the tarmac to fire off a round of press-ups before the race in a new warm-up routine.
The Ducati rider then flexed his muscles on his bike, biding his time behind Martin before making his move in lap 11.
Martin said he had "a good package to fight for the rest of the season" but admitted that Marquez was the better rider on the day.
"I think today to win was really difficult," said Martin.
"It was one of the days when I rode almost perfectly, I was really smooth, really confident, and even then I couldn't win," he added.
It was Marquez's sixth Grand Prix win of the season, despite missing the races in Le Mans and Catalonia to undergo surgery on his foot and shoulder.
A sunny day in Japan clouded over and cooled considerably shortly before the race but the rain held off.
Marquez never looked in any trouble once he had gone past Martin, who in turn looked comfortable in second place.
Bezzecchi had to fight a furious rearguard action to hold off fellow Italia Enea Bastianini, who finished fourth.
Spain's Pedro Acosta, who chalked up his first ever victory in MotoGP in Austria, finished seventh.
Ai Ogura, who was bidding to become the first Japanese race winner in Motegi since 2004, was sixth.
Brazil's Diogo Moreira, who finished second in the sprint when Martin was demoted to third due to a penalty, crashed out of the grand prix.
fa96c7ff71bca681: SEPANG, Oct 4 — The Bahrain Grand Prix is now scheduled to start at 4.33pm today after torrential rain forced Formula One officials to repeatedly delay proceedings at the Sepang International Circuit.
The race had originally been due to start at 3pm local time, but a heavy downpour swept across the circuit shortly before lights out and left conditions unsuitable for racing.
Race Control initially announced a delayed start because of “excessive rain”, with no immediate replacement time given.
A revised formation lap was later scheduled for 3.40pm, but the weather continued to disrupt proceedings before officials eventually set a new race start time of 4.33pm.
The prolonged delay has left pole-sitter Max Verstappen and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton waiting to lead the field away from the front row.
Verstappen secured pole for Red Bull in qualifying yesterday, with Hamilton alongside him after producing a late lap to claim his first front-row start since Barcelona.
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is due to start third for Mercedes following a five-place grid penalty for Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar.
Torrential rain arrived about 20 minutes before the original scheduled start, halting preparations as standing water accumulated around the circuit.
The wet weather has added another complication to a weekend already marked by low grip and heavy tyre degradation at Sepang.
Pirelli had earlier pointed to the circuit’s dusty and abrasive surface as contributing to increased sliding and tyre wear.
Barring any further intervention from Race Control, the field is now due to get under way at 4.33pm.
b1ff53f8ae507a7b: PUTRAJAYA: Germany's Lennart Jasch clinched his first professional general classification (GC) title as the Le Tour de Langkawi (LTdL) concluded with Stage Eight from Muar to Putrajaya today.
The Tudor Pro Cycling Team rider completed the eight-stage race in 28 hours, 57 minutes and two seconds, finishing 26 seconds ahead of Caja Rural-Seguros RGA's Abel Balderstone.
Jasch's teammate Jan Castellon was third, 42 seconds behind.
The 26-year-old also secured the polka dot jersey as king of the mountains with 45 points, ahead of Wheeltop Rotor Chengdu Team's Petr Rikunov (41) and Castellon (26).
"I am very happy. It was another really difficult day. On paper, it might have looked easy, but it certainly was not, especially the last seven or eight kilometres.
"I am very grateful to the team and for all the support throughout the week. We should all be very proud of our performance," said the former ice skater.
Jasch arrived in Malaysia as a new professional targeting a top-five finish, but his Stage Two victory at Gunung Jerai changed the team's expectations.
"I came with high hopes and even higher ambitions, but actually winning here was something we could hardly believe.
"We thought perhaps I could finish in the top five. Then, after I won the second stage, we began to realise that perhaps I was the strongest rider," he said.
The victory was also his first outside Europe, making his week in Malaysia particularly memorable.
"This means a lot. It is my first professional GC win and the first time I have won a race outside Italy."
Jasch had already made LTdL history by becoming the first rider to win a stage finishing at Gunung Jerai. He held the orange leader's jersey from Stage Two until the finish.
"Now I know I can be a good GC rider. I had hoped that before, but I needed to prove it," he added.

XDS Astana's Matteo Malucelli won the 188.3km final stage in four hours, five minutes and 17 seconds, ahead of Modern Adventure Pro Cycling's Riley Pickrell, who clocked the same time. Team Picnic PostNL's Christian Rees finished third.
Malucelli also secured the sprint classification with 64 points, followed by Pickrell (57) and Nil Gimeno (22).
Aisan Racing Team's Yuhi Todome topped the Asian rider classification in 29:04:23, while Tsen Ren Bao was the highest-placed Malaysian in 25th overall.
01818381dcca45a3: KUANTAN: The upcoming Melaka election could serve as an indicator of whether the 16th General Election (GE16) will be called earlier, said the Council of Former Elected Representatives (Mubarak).
Its president, Tan Sri Abdul Aziz Abdul Rahman, said the current political momentum and Barisan Nasional's strength could be factors influencing the timing of the next general election.
"GE16 needs to be held sooner, given BN's current strength. However, we will have to see what happens in Melaka... the Melaka election will serve as an indicator of the timing of GE16.
"If BN walks away with a victory, then the general election could be pushed back until the end of the term," he told reporters after Mubarak's 23rd annual general meeting here.
BN secured victories in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections held this year and is looking to retain Melaka, where it won 21 out of 28 seats in the previous state election.
The Election Commission is scheduled to meet on Oct 7 to decide on the nomination and polling dates for the Melaka election.

On the possibility of cooperation between Umno and Pas in GE16, Aziz said it would ultimately be a "game of numbers", with both parties needing to assess their respective strengths and field winnable candidates.
"If Umno and Pas can work together and combine their strengths, then go ahead. Once you are already in power, you can decide who you want to bring in (parties to work together with)," he said.
Meanwhile, he said it was high time for the country to create three deputy prime minister posts, with one each representing Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
"Sabah and Sarawak are quite financially independent and have a lot of resources, so it is not proper to leave them out of the mainstream administration.
"This move is to create inclusiveness and a sense of collective leadership, rather than having the administration dominated by leaders from Peninsular Malaysia," he said.
Malaysia currently has two deputy prime ministers — Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.
Fadillah is the first deputy prime minister from East Malaysia.
f80cbb4c685ac634: KUALA LUMPUR: Rising star Mhia Firdaus has etched her name in the history books as the first Malay actor to secure a nomination at the prestigious 63rd Golden Horse Awards, set to take place in Taipei, Taiwan this November.
The 20-year-old talent earned a nod in the Best Supporting Actress category for her poignant portrayal of a deaf girl in the upcoming film Sayang Sayang, which arrives in local cinemas on Nov 5.
Taking to Instagram to express her emotion, Mhia admitted that she was still coming to terms with the landmark achievement.
"Still trying to process all of this. I am deeply honoured and grateful to be nominated for Best Supporting Actress at the 63rd Golden Horse Awards," she wrote.
"This is something I never imagined for myself and I feel incredibly blessed to be given this opportunity."
Mhia, who is the daughter of acclaimed actress Farah Ahmad and granddaughter of legendary screen icon Datuk Fauziah Nawi, dedicated the achievement to her closest family members.

"First and foremost, to my mama, sister, and brother, thank you for always being there for me, believing in me, and supporting me every step of the way. Having you by my side makes this moment all the more meaningful," she shared.
She was equally quick to credit the creative team behind the camera for their dedication and trust throughout production.

"To my director, fellow cast members, and crew, thank you for your trust, guidance, hard work, and for bringing this story to life. This nomination would not have been possible without every single person who was part of this journey," she noted, adding her heartfelt thanks to supporters who have encouraged her along the way.

Calling the recognition the biggest milestone of her career thus far, Mhia reflected on the significance of joining Asia's cinematic elite: "This nomination is already such a meaningful milestone in my acting journey and I am profoundly grateful to be part of the 63rd Golden Horse Awards. Thank you for this extraordinary recognition."

A joint Malaysian-Taiwanese production directed by Tang Hsiang-Chu and executive produced by Yeh Jufeng and Jin Ong, Sayang Sayang features an international ensemble of over 100 cast and crew members from Malaysia, Taiwan, and India.
The cast includes Taiwanese star Lee Lee-Zen and rising talent Sasha Tang, alongside Malaysian performers Jo Kukathas, Nandagopall Mohan, Ong Ai Leng, and Amir Ahnaf.

The film secured four additional nominations at the 63rd Golden Horse Awards, including Best Original Screenplay (Tang Hsiang-Chu), Best New Performer (Nandagopall Mohan), Best Sound Effects (Wu Shu-Yao, Hsu Chiao-Han, and Liu Pei-Min), and Best Visual Effects (Tomi Kuo, Ivan Lin, and Hannah Han).
In her category, Mhia faces competition from Audrey Lin (Girl), Sun Jialing (Big Little Things), Judy Ongg (Sunshine Women's Choir), and Kearen Pang (We Are Born Good).
The winners will be announced at the grand awards ceremony on Nov 22 at the Taipei Music Centre.
913fc283182f2f6d: Decades before the modern web, the BBC Domesday Project dared to archive an entire nation using…. what else – massive LV-ROM (LaserVision Read Only Memory) LaserDiscs. To mark the impending 40th anniversary of the BBC Domesday Project's release, the UK's Centre for Computing History (CCH) hosted a celebration at its museum on September 19, bringing together several of the original team members responsible for the system. One was Mike Tibbetts, an assistant to Peter Armstrong, the BBC producer behind the project. Tibbetts revealed that the UK's domestic intelligence service, MI5, took an interest in the system, but "they didn't understand a word of what we were doing!" "And on one occasion, Peter and I had to give a presentation, or Peter gave the presentation to [former prime minister] Margaret Thatcher, and well, I'm not sure she understood what we were doing either…" What they were doing was compiling a trove of data that will prove invaluable to historians in the years to come, even if the politicians of the era looked nervously on at the amount of data being handed over to the public. The Domesday Project was intended to be a modern version of the Domesday Book, compiled after the 1066 Norman invasion of England. The original book surveyed most of England and parts of Wales and was used by the King to assess dues owed to him. 900 years later, the name was given to a project in which more than a million people participated to provide a snapshot of life in the UK. Participants (many of whom were school children) contributed content, which was linked with maps, photographs, and other data. It was all compiled onto a pair of LaserDiscs – the Community Disc and the National Disc – and accessed via a BBC Master computer and a Philips VP415 LaserVision player. Armstrong came up with the idea, and the team compiled the project between 1984 and 1986. The system was eventually released at the end of 1986, and was aimed at schools, libraries, and universities. It was, alas, not a roaring sales success – the exact price per unit is difficult to pin down, but approximately £5,000 is a fair estimate. Government subsidies lowered the cost to around £3,000, but it was still out of reach for much of its audience. As a resource, however, it has huge value, which will only increase as the years pass. Tibbetts drew parallels to the original Domesday Book, which took centuries for historians to recognize as a vital resource. "Perhaps," he mused, "40 years is simply too short a time for historians to perceive the Domesday Project as a sufficiently distant benchmark of useful research." Perhaps. However, while hundreds of years have passed since the Domesday Book was compiled, the years have not been kind to the Domesday Project, thanks to technology's inexorable march. "The original Domesday Book had one huge advantage over the Domesday Project when it comes to future-proofing and longevity," explained Tibbetts. "The vellum pages of the original Domesday have been preserved for 940 years so far, and it's likely to continue to exist well into the future. "It took very few years for the bespoke technology of the BBC Domesday Project to be overtaken by universal media technologies." However, they chose the technology at the time for good technical reasons. The BBC Micro could output a 625-line television picture. The Philips LaserVision system could be re-engineered to store alphanumeric data. There wasn't much in the way of authoring and playback systems, so, as Tibbetts explained, the team had to invent everything. "In technological terms," he said, "the world of 1984 really couldn't be more different from the instant-access, media-rich world of today." And so, inevitably, within a few short years, that technology began to show its age. "As was entirely predictable, our discs aged and became difficult to read. The expensive LV-ROM player was quickly superseded by cheaper and more widely available CD-ROM and DVD systems." And, worse, "Largely because of the lack of any great academic interest in preserving our massive resource for the future, the BBC Domesday Project was in grave danger of disappearing without a trace." Several initiatives have kicked off over the years to preserve the project, and the CCH's event was as much about celebrating those as it was about looking at the project's genesis. Tibbetts dropped some nuggets of information about the project, estimating that 60 people reported directly to him and Armstrong, with another 60 in subcontracted teams. He also discussed the frustration the team felt as doubt was cast about whether the project was even possible. "We came back from Christmas in January 1986," Tibbetts recalled, "we sat down for our first team meeting, and I was forced to point out that our little VAX minicomputer didn't have one byte of data that was ready to go onto the Domesday discs, so we did the whole thing in a few months!" As far as hardware was concerned, Andy Finney, who handled mastering the discs, remembered that the original plan for the Domesday Project was for it to be mouse-based, rather than the trackball the system used for navigation. The mouse was still a relatively novel concept, alien to many users. "I remember vividly one chap who was navigating with this mouse on the table, and he moved the mouse towards him, and by the time he got to the edge of the table, he hadn't actually reached the bottom of the screen. So he went on the edge and underneath…" Tibbetts added, "I always feel guilty about the mouse, because we got that wrong … the decision came down in favor of the trackball because that is much more easy for somebody with movement disabilities to use rather than a mouse." "But boy, did we get that wrong…" As Tibbetts noted, even with little interest from some parts of the academic community, enthusiasts have continued to put in a huge amount of effort over the years to keep the resource accessible. Simon Inns of the Domesday86 project described it as "a race against time" – not just for hardware, but to get data off discs before bit rot rendered them unreadable. The good news is that the Domesday discs have been preserved, and reside in the Internet Archive. "Anyone," said Inns, "can go to the Internet Archive and download a Domesday Disc. This is, like, groundbreaking stuff. 10 years ago, this was a laugh, right? Now you can actually do this." While there might not be many functioning examples of the hardware around anymore, the preservation efforts mean that the Domesday Project will endure. "Our hope," said Inns, "is that within the next couple of years, everyone in this room [at The Centre for Computing History] will be able to have a Domesday system and be able to experience what it was like." ®
53488c1abd95954c: SEPANG: The Bahrain Grand Prix (GP), initially delayed by heavy rain and standing water on the track, was halted for a second time after the formation lap at 3.40pm on Sunday.
Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who took pole position on Saturday, was able to pull away behind the Safety Car for two formation laps.
However, several issues emerged. Verstappen briefly struggled with power, as did Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto.
Red Bull's Isack Hadjar slid into the gravel, while Lando Norris narrowly avoided doing the same.
Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton suffered the biggest setback after losing power, forcing several cars to overtake him.
Ferrari said the problem was caused by a software issue and managed to reset the system, allowing Hamilton to regain power.
Hamilton had dropped to the back of the field because of the issue.
The disruption left the pit-lane order jumbled, but the FIA later confirmed that the original grid order would be restored.
Hamilton will therefore start second when the race resumes.04:34 PM
febf7d084d7fecfe: SEPANG: The return of Formula 1 to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after a nine-year absence received special attention today when His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, attended the 2026 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race, together with the top leaders of Malaysia, Bahrain and Brunei.
His Majesty was received on arrival at about 2.15pm by Bahrain Crown Prince sand Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Also attending the race were the Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, and Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, who were received by Anwar at about 2.35pm.

The Raja Muda of Selangor, Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah; the Tunku Mahkota of Kedah, Tunku Shazuddin Ariff Sultan Sallehuddin; and the Tengku Mahkota of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; also attended the race, marking the return of the roar of F1 engines to Sepang after the last race was held there in 2017.
The race, scheduled to start at 3 pm, was slightly delayed due to heavy rain after Negaraku and the Bahrain national anthem were played.
The event is expected to attract nearly 100,000 spectators and will also feature a fly-past by Gulf Air aircraft before the race gets underway.

Four-time world champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull Racing will start the 56-lap race from pole position, followed by seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari and current championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes-AMG Petronas.

In July, F1 confirmed Malaysia as the host venue for the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), and the Malaysian and Bahraini governments.

F1's return to Malaysia followed discussions and cooperation involving His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim and Bahrain's King Hamad bin Isa Al-Khalifa, as well as the two governments, to retain the Bahrain Grand Prix on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia previously hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix at SIC from 1999 to 2017 before the race was dropped from the F1 calendar. — BERNAMA
c01576b422eac4cc: KUALA LUMPUR: Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur mengetepikan perjanjian fi antara sebuah firma guaman dan 203 anak guam dalam satu kes pelaburan, selepas memutuskan perjanjian itu tidak dicapai secara adil serta mengandungi terma tidak munasabah.

Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman Nixon Kennedy Kumbong, turut memerintahkan semua 18 fi guaman dikeluarkan Tetuan Jerald Gomez & Associates berjumlah RM1.55 juta ditaksirkan memandangkan tiada perjanjian fi dimeterai.
Dalam istilah kehakiman, 'taksir' bermaksud proses penilaian secara rasmi oleh mahkamah bagi menentu atau menetapkan jumlah sebenar kos atau fi guaman yang wajar dibayar.
Nixon mengarahkan pendaftar Mahkamah Tinggi mengendalikan proses penaksiran berkenaan.
Beliau juga memerintahkan firma berkenaan memulangkan mana-mana jumlah didapati telah dibayar melebihi amaun penaksiran dalam tempoh 30 hari dari tarikh sijil penaksiran dikeluarkan.

Plaintif, yang merupakan pelabur secara kolektif mengalami kerugian kewangan yang cukup besar dalam satu skim pelaburan yang dikaitkan dengan pengasas bersama MYAirline, Goh Hwan Hua, dan telah melantik firma guaman tersebut mengambil tindakan perundangan.
Firma tersebut telah menjalankan siasatan awal, mengadakan beberapa perjumpaan dengan bakal penuntut, dan akhirnya memfailkan writ dan penyataan tuntutan bagi pihak mereka.
Plaintif telah mencabar terma dan syarat pelantikan yang ditandatangani pada 16 Jan 2024 mengikut Seksyen 116, 118, 126 dan 128 Akta Profesion Undang-undang 1976.
Plaintif memohon mengetepikan atau meminda perjanjian itu, pelanjutan tempoh bagi mengemukakan proses penaksiran, serta mendapatkan perintah lanjutan untuk penaksiran esemua 18 fi guaman berkenaan.
Antara isu dipertimbangkan adalah sama ada perjanjian itu telah dicapai secara adil berasaskan siri pertemuan antara pihak bekenaan sebelum ditandatangani.

Mahkamah turut meneliti sama ada terma terkandung munasabah, termasuk struktur kadar bayaran mengikut jam, ketiadaan had maksimum fi, dan anggaran firma terbabit yang menjangkakan fi guaman mencapai kira-kira RM5 juta.

Plaintif membangkitkan kebimbangan mengenai caj dikenakan, antaranya kadar RM2,000 sejam bagi tugasan dilakukan individu yang belum diterima secara rasmi sebagai peguam cara dan peguam bela, RM160,100 bagi kehadiran lapan kakitangan pada satu sidang media, serta RM58,500 bagi kehadiran seorang peguam dalam 11 pertemuan.
Mereka mendakwa berlakunya pengagihan kakitangan secara berlebihan, pertindihan kerja, serta ketiadaan rekod masa dibuat secara masa nyata.
Dalam penghakiman 43 halaman itu, Nixon menegaskan keadilan sesuatu perjanjian perlu dinilai berasaskan sifat fidusiari dalam hubungan antara peguam cara dan anak guam.

Beliau memutuskan plaintif berjaya membuktikan kes mengikut Seksyen 118 Profesion Undang-undang 1976, dan turut memutuskan klausa penyelesaian perselisihan alternatif dalam perjanjian fi berkenaan melanggar Seksyen 118.
“Terma pelantikan bertarikh 16 Jan 2024 (dengan ini) diketepikan,” katanya.
Jared Tee dan Syed Afiq Syed Albakri bertindak bagi pihak plaintif, manakala Michelle Wong dan David Dev Peter mewakili firma guaman tersebut.
d821e7783bbfd9f8: PETALING JAYA: Acclaimed British-American sitarist Anoushka Shankar has announced an impromptu show at the Temple of Fine Arts in Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur after a scheduled performance at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre was cancelled at the last minute.
Anoushka said the new event, expected to take place at 8pm, is in no way connected to the promoter of the original show.
“Seats are strictly limited and allocated on a first-come, first-served basis to valid ticket holders of the original performance only.
“It does not replace your ticket refund, which will be processed separately as previously communicated,” she said in a Facebook post.
She said her team had arranged the event at the Temple of Fine Arts, but warned that the venue is considerably smaller than the original one, urging attendees to arrive early to secure entry.

She also thanked the Temple of Fine Arts and local sitarist and composer Kumar Karthigesu for helping with the new arrangement, as well as her band and crew for “pulling out all the stops” saying, “It takes a village”.

04d4bc6f9e64d6f9: PETALING JAYA: A Perlis-based freelance motivational speaker linked to an alleged sexual harassment allegation has been rearrested after police received another report against him, this time from a 19-year-old woman.

Hamzah said the latest case was being investigated under Section 509 of the Penal Code, which deals with acts or words intended to insult a person's modesty or intrude on their privacy, and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, which covers the improper use of communications networks.

Police are also investigating the case under Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955, which deals with indecent, threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour likely to cause a breach of the peace.

Section 509 carries a sentence of up to five years' jail, a fine, or both, while Section 233 provides for a maximum RM500,000 fine, up to two years' imprisonment, or both, upon conviction. Section 14 carries a maximum RM100 fine.
Hamzah said the suspect will be brought to the Kangar magistrates' court tomorrow for a fresh remand order.

9b45c67418533b52: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Former law minister Datuk Zaid Ibrahim says Sarawak premier Abang Johari Openg’s assurance that Petros will not undermine Petronas rings hollow while the state oil company seeks a bigger role in the gas business and Sarawak continues to question the federal legal framework governing petroleum.
Writing on Facebook, Zaid said the central issue was Petros’s desire to take over the gas aggregator role currently performed by Petronas in Sarawak.

That role is integral to the gas value chain, he said, and cannot be transferred without affecting Petronas’s commercial position. He estimated Petronas’s Sarawak gas business at about RM10 billion annually.

Zaid said the impact was already visible in the confusion created by competing claims over payments. He pointed to the Shell dispute, saying roughly RM80 million a month had been withheld while the parties disputed who should be paid.

Abang Johari had said earlier that Petros’s expansion was not designed to displace Petronas. He said Sarawak would continue to work with Petronas while developing its ability to process gas locally and move into higher-value downstream activities.

His comments followed Petros’s joint development agreement with Norwegian company Höegh Evi for a Kuching LNG regasification terminal, which is expected to be operational by 2029. Sarawak is also exploring small-scale LNG facilities and carbon capture, utilisation and storage projects.

Zaid said those ambitions need not be incompatible with Sarawak’s development, but the order of discussion mattered. The state must first recognise Petronas’s rights over Malaysia’s oil and gas under the Petroleum Development Act 1974, he said.

He noted that Sarawak was challenging the application of the PDA and other federal petroleum laws in the state. That, he said, was a challenge to the legal foundation of Petronas, rather than a routine negotiation over commercial participation.
Once the legal position is accepted, Zaid said, the parties can negotiate a role for Petros that addresses Sarawak’s circumstances without dismantling key functions of the national oil company.

He warned that the consequences would extend beyond Sarawak if other producing states pursued similar claims. Petronas would lose the scale that supports its national role, including its ability to invest and contribute to federal revenue, he said.

3d8988766620548b: KUALA LUMPUR: The Kuala Lumpur High Court has set aside a fee agreement between a law firm and 203 clients in an investment case, ruling that it was not fairly obtained and contained unreasonable terms.
Judicial commissioner Nixon Kennedy Kumbong also ordered all 18 legal bills issued by Messrs Jerald Gomez & Associates, totalling RM1.55 million, to be taxed as if there had been no fee agreement.
In court terms, "tax" means to officially assess, determine, or fix the exact amount of legal costs or fees owed in a lawsuit.
Nixon directed the High Court registrar to conduct the taxation.
He also ordered the firm to refund any amount found to have been paid in excess of the taxed sum within 30 days of the certificate of taxation being issued.

The plaintiffs, who were investors, collectively suffered substantial financial losses in an investment scheme associated with MYAirline co-founder Goh Hwan Hua and had appointed the legal firm to pursue legal recourse.
The firm carried out preliminary investigations, held several meetings with prospective claimants, and eventually filed a writ and statement of claim on their behalf.
The plaintiffs had challenged the terms of engagement signed on Jan 16, 2024, under Sections 116, 118, 126 and 128 of the Legal Profession Act 1976.
They sought to have the agreement set aside or varied, to extend the time to invoke the taxation process, and to obtain consequential orders for the taxation of the 18 bills.
Among the issues considered was whether the agreement had been fairly obtained in view of meetings between the parties before it was signed.
The court also examined whether its terms were reasonable, including the hourly rate structure, the absence of a fee cap, and the firm's estimate of about RM5 million in legal fees.

The plaintiffs had raised concerns over charges including RM2,000 an hour for work carried out by a person not called to the Bar, RM160,100 for eight personnel attending a press conference, and RM58,500 for a lawyer's attendance at 11 meetings.
They alleged over-staffing, duplication of work, and the absence of contemporaneous time records.
In his 43-page judgment, Nixon said the fairness of the agreement had to be assessed in light of the fiduciary nature of the solicitor-client relationship.
He concluded that the plaintiffs had made out their case under Section 118 of the Act, and also ruled that the alternative dispute resolution clause in the fee agreement contravened Section 118.
“The terms of engagement dated Jan 16, 2024, (are) to be set aside,” he said.
Jared Tee and Syed Afiq Syed Albakri appeared for the plaintiffs, while Michelle Wong and David Dev Peter represented the legal firm.
55c4c0c5549c8a98: NEW DELHI: Indian police launched an investigation on Sunday into allegations of sexual harassment against officers during protests in the capital against the country's election commission.

11a88d84832a0764: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) is tracking down individuals and groups offering illegal motorcycle ride-hailing services to transport visitors and spectators attending the Formula One (F1) Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).

According to Berita Harian, the operators were found advertising their services through various social media platforms, offering rides from several locations to the circuit grounds and between SIC and nearby parking areas.

The report also found touts offering rides for as much as RM80 for a 10-kilometre journey from Mitsui Outlet Park to a Petronas station near the main entrance of the circuit. Some operators were also said to provide helmets for passengers.

While the services have attracted visitors looking for a faster alternative to traffic-clogged roads, concerns have been raised over safety risks, particularly in the event of accidents or other unforeseen incidents.

The enforcement comes amid an influx of spectators attending the F1 Bahrain Grand Prix, with traffic congestion around the Sepang circuit area drawing widespread attention over the weekend.
eaaedfadfab6f70d: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the timing of his resignation, which will take effect once former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pays the RM50 million fine, was agreed with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when he tendered his resignation.

"Of course, people say that it's an act, political, and so on. But I'm sticking my head out — the moment he returns, I have to quit. I am not wishy-washy or dilly-dally. He goes home. I leave," said Loke, who is the transport minister, in an interview with The Straits Times.

Loke announced on Sept 19 that he would quit the Cabinet in protest against Najib being allowed to serve the remainder of his graft sentence under house arrest, following the Pardons Board's decision to grant him the arrangement.
Loke said his decision illustrated the balancing act between staying in power and holding to principles that the party says it cannot abandon.
He submitted his resignation to Anwar on Sept 28.
However, his clarification on Sept 29 that his resignation would only take effect once Najib pays the RM50 million fine drew criticism.
On Sept 18, Najib was granted house arrest for the remainder of his sentence, subject to his paying the RM50 million fine imposed following his conviction in the SRC International case.

Meanwhile, in the interview, the Seremban MP acknowledged that while DAP continues to command strong support among Chinese voters, this alone is insufficient to deliver federal power, with growing disappointment among its core electorate remaining a concern.
Loke said DAP would never take Chinese support "for granted", but added that the party must build consensus with its coalition partners.
"We know sometimes it's frustrating to be in this kind of situation, but that is the reality of Malaysian politics.
"There is no way for DAP to form a government on its own without working with others.
This is a reality we must accept: We can only push as far as possible, relying on objective and persuasive arguments to get things done within the system," he said.

That pragmatism also extends to DAP's potential partners after the 16th General Election, with Loke saying the party's door remains open despite opposition among some grassroots members to parties such as Pas, Umno and Bersatu.
He pointed to DAP's decision to work with Umno after the 2022 general election to form the Anwar-led federal government as evidence that political alliances can shift according to circumstances.
"I don't close my doors to anyone. I hold this belief that we have come to a point that politics has to be agile.
"Of course, not without any principle or any precondition, because it depends on the circumstances what is best for the country to move forward."
Loke also remained confident that the Malay unity narrative promoted by Umno and Pas would not be sustainable.

"Negeri Sembilan's defeat is basically a blessing in disguise for us. They (Umno-Pas) talked about Malay unity and forming a formidable state government to resolve the royal impasse. What decision did they make? They dethroned the state ruler.
"Right now, Malays elsewhere in the entire country can see that an Umno-Pas government did this.
"So that's why I said DAP is being spared this burden right now. In a way, the Malay unity momentum cannot necessarily be sustained in terms of electoral trends."

2db23289cfd16d95: LONDON/MOSCOW: The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allied oil producers (OPEC+) is set to keep oil production targets steady for November, three sources close to the matter said ahead of the group's meeting on Sunday.

Gulf OPEC+ producers have been pumping well below output targets amid continuing export disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran, with exports fluctuating at 60-80 per cent of normal levels in recent months.

The war has also delayed the group's output capacity review, which is crucial to determining members' 2027 output quotas, as it has thrown estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, industry sources have said.

The OPEC+ group, comprising the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia, has agreed in principle to keep targets steady for November, the three sources close to the talks said.
OPEC+ has been raising output targets for much of 2026 after years of production cuts, but most of the increases remained on paper because of the Middle East conflict.
The seven core OPEC+ members pumped 25 million barrels per day in August, up 630,000 bpd from July, yet still roughly 5 million bpd below pre-war levels in February, OPEC data shows.

OPEC+ still has about 2 million bpd of output cuts in place covering most members. It needs a capacity review to decide how to distribute increases, and any changes to output are unlikely before 2027, sources have said.
The group's seven core members meeting on Sunday are Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman.

fa24f3d63961e810: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — As Malaysia’s creative industry continues to step into the international spotlight, the year marked another chapter of achievements, putting its homegrown stories, talent and productions firmly on the regional map.

The latest recognition came from the 2026 Asian Academy Creative Awards (AACA), which announced its National Winners on September 30, with several Malaysian titles across film, television and animation among those recognised.
The AACA is a regional awards programme recognising excellence in film, television and digital content across the Asia-Pacific.
The awards follow a two-stage process.
Entries first compete at the national level, with the winners advancing to the Grand Awards to compete against winners from across the region.
Malaysia’s 2026 National Winners will represent the country at the Grand Awards Gala on December 3 at Capitol Theatre in Singapore where the overall winners will be announced.
The spotlight on Astro film and television
This year’s Astro productions featured prominently among the Malaysian winners, led by Astro Shaw’s feature film Malam Terlarang, which secured four awards.
The film won Best Feature Film, Best Direction (Feature Film) for the late Nurhanisham Muhammad, Best Actress in a Supporting Role for actress Sofia Jane, and Best Promo or Trailer.

Astro Originals series Good Boys Go To Heaven also picked up five awards, including Best Drama Series, Best Actor in a Leading Role for Beto Kusyairy, Best Cinematography (Fiction), Best Editing and Best Screenplay.
Meanwhile, Bad Cop won Best Adaptation of an Existing Format (Scripted).
Datuk Aznil Haji Nawawi secured two awards — Best Non-Scripted Entertainment and Best Entertainment Host/Presenter as part of Talk To My Manager programme.

Other Astro-linked winners included Astro KUDADA CNY Countdown Gala 2026, which won Best General Entertainment, Game or Quiz Programme; and Astro Star Quest 2025, which won Best Music or Dance Programme.

Other Malaysian productions also picked up awards, with Life In A Loop winning Best Short-Form Content, Kerikil Depan Pintu taking Best Single Drama/Telemovie/Anthology Episode, and Sujud Terakhir Encik Norman winning Best Visual or Special FX in a TV Series or Feature Film.
Viu Malaysia achievements
Viu Malaysia secured five National Wins through its Viu Original productions, covering acting, directing, music, and short-form storytelling.
Seadanya Kita earned two awards: Emma Maembong won Best Actress in a Leading Role and its official theme song Berakhir Kita, took Best Theme Song or Title Theme.

ad6ecec0ec83089f: KUALA LUMPUR: The pursuit of Olympic gold should not come at the expense of the Asian Games, says sports analyst Datuk Dr Pekan Ramli.

He questioned BA of Malaysia's (BAM) approach after Malaysia's badminton squad returned from Aichi-Nagoya with only a women's doubles bronze through Pearly Tan–M Thinaah, falling short of the official one-silver, one-bronze target.
BAM president Tengku Zafrul Abdul Aziz had said the association also set specific internal targets for its Asian Games squad.
However, Pearly–Thinaah were the only Malaysian shuttlers to reach the podium.
Pekan said the campaign was disappointing and questioned whether the association and players showed sufficient hunger for medals at the continental Games.
"We should take the Asian Games seriously. Are we interested only in the Olympics?" he said.
"From what I saw, our players did not seem hungry enough for medals at the Asian Games.
"That is my impression of the mentality of the association and the players."
Malaysia suffered early exits across the other individual events.
Men's singles players Leong Jun Hao and Justin Hoh bowed out in the last 16, while women's singles representatives Wong Ling Ching and K Letshanaa exited in the second and first rounds respectively.
The men's doubles challenge also ended in the second round, with Goh Sze Fei–Nur Izzuddin Rumsani and Aaron Chia–Tee Kai Wun both eliminated.
Mixed doubles pairs Goh Soon Huat–Shevon Lai and Chen Tang Jie–Cheng Su Yin suffered second-round exits, while both Malaysian teams fell in the quarter-finals.
Pekan urged BAM to look beyond world rankings when setting medal objectives, arguing that every player should carry responsibility for delivering.
"It is not just about rankings. Being world No. 1 does not guarantee a gold medal. Someone ranked lower can also win," he said.
"We must give them an assignment - fight for gold or fight seriously for a medal, regardless of their ranking."
He warned that concentrating expectations on the highest-ranked players could leave others feeling less accountable for their performances.
Pekan also questioned what he perceived as greater urgency only when the Olympics approached, saying expectations should be enforced consistently.
"Only when the Olympics approach do we start pushing our players, including those in RTG," he said.
"We need to set clear key performance indicators for the players and enforce them.
"If they fail to meet those targets, we should consider leaving them out of tournaments," he said.

85b3efb7d6266df9: KUALA BERANG, Oct 4 — A man suspected of murdering his elder brother in Kampung Banggol Tasek, Bukit Payong, Marang yesterday has been remanded for seven days from today until Oct 10.

In the incident at about 9 am yesterday, a 43-year-old man died after allegedly being struck with a blunt object.
The victim’s 36-year-old sister was also injured and is warded at HSNZ after she allegedly tried to prevent the suspect from attacking the victim.

Terengganu police chief Datuk Mohd Khairi Khairudin said today that dissatisfaction with his elder brother, who allegedly frequently asked their parents for money, is believed to have led to the fatal attack. — Bernama
37b293d839335219: SEPANG, Oct 4 — The start of the Bahrain Grand Prix was delayed today after torrential rain swept across Sepang just minutes before lights out, leaving pole-sitter Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton waiting for conditions to improve.
Race Control confirmed that the Formula One race, scheduled to begin at 3pm, could not start on time after the circuit was hit by a heavy downpour roughly 20 minutes before the scheduled start.
“Delayed start due to excessive rain,” Race Control said in a brief announcement.
No revised start time was immediately given, with teams and drivers forced to wait for further instructions as standing water built up around the Sepang International Circuit.
According to media reports, the announcement confirmed a delay rather than a cancellation, with the race awaiting improved conditions.
Verstappen is due to start from pole position for Red Bull alongside Ferrari’s Hamilton, who secured his first front-row start since Barcelona in qualifying yesterday.
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli will line up third for Mercedes after Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar, who qualified ahead of him, was handed a five-place grid penalty.
The sudden downpour has added another layer of uncertainty to a weekend already dominated by high temperatures, low grip and significant tyre degradation.
Pirelli had earlier identified Sepang’s dusty and abrasive surface as a factor behind increased tyre sliding and wear, with lap times running slower than expected during practice.
Teams must now wait for Race Control to determine when conditions are safe enough for the starting procedure to resume.

1e775213abd9722e: PETALING JAYA: A proposal to give the opposition leader a role in determining the Dewan Rakyat’s agenda has drawn mixed reaction from government bloc leaders, with Amanah rejecting it while a PKR MP wants further consideration.

Amanah secretary-general Faiz Fadzil said there is no need to implement the proposal at this juncture, while Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Karim welcomed the move and called for it to be referred to a parliamentary select committee.

Faiz said although similar practices exist in several developed countries, this approach is unsuitable for Malaysia because the opposition has yet to demonstrate sufficient maturity in carrying out checks and balances.
“Although countries such as the UK and Canada practise this, the opposition there is genuinely mature in carrying out its role as an effective check and balance,” he told FMT.

Faiz cited the decision by some opposition MPs to walk out of the Dewan Rakyat during the debate on the royal commission of inquiry into Tabung Haji, leaving only government representatives and several opposition MPs taking part.

He also questioned the opposition’s decision to first appoint Kemaman MP Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, a PAS vice-president and PN chairman, as opposition leader before returning the post to Larut MP Hamzah Zainudin, despite PAS being the largest opposition bloc.
He said the opposition also failed to table an alternative budget, as is commonly done in several developed countries, although Pakatan Harapan did so when it was in opposition.

On Friday, Wawasan secretary-general Saifuddin Abdullah proposed that the opposition leader be given a role in determining the Dewan Rakyat’s agenda as part of efforts to strengthen consultation in the democratic system.
The Indera Mahkota MP said the approach is among reforms that should be considered in the system, institutions, leadership and government.
Hassan said the Dewan Rakyat Standing Orders would need to be amended if the opposition leader were given a role in determining Parliament’s agenda.
He said the agenda is currently determined largely by the prime minister as leader of the House, with some procedural matters handled by the Dewan Rakyat speaker.
He also said the change could strengthen the checks and balances process and enhance government accountability.
In additiion, it would bolster Parliament’s independence under the Parliamentary Service Act and strengthen the separation of powers between the executive and legislative branches.
d6b90505bbd2af69: GEORGE TOWN: Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup (KPDN) Pulau Pinang, sedang menyiasat dakwaan beberapa kenderaan mengalami masalah selepas mengisi bahan api di stesen minyak berhampiran Batu Kawan.

“Pihak KPDN Pulau Pinang mengambil maklum berkenaan dakwaan berlaku masalah pada kenderaan selepas mengisi minyak di stesen minyak, berdekatan Batu Kawan.
“KPDN Pulau Pinang akan menghantar satu pasukan untuk meneliti perkara ini dan akan berkongsi kenyataan media selepas itu,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

Terdahulu, beberapa hantaran di media sosial tular, apabila pengguna mendakwa kenderaan mereka mengalami masalah termasuk gagal dihidupkan, selepas mengisi minyak di beberapa stesen minyak di sekitar Pulau Pinang.
Hantaran itu turut mendakwa masalah berkenaan disyaki berpunca daripada bahan api bercampur air, namun perkara itu belum disahkan oleh pihak berkuasa.

70a4ab0ecce5f0c0: PETALING JAYA: Acclaimed British-American sitarist Anoushka Shankar announced a last-minute cancellation of her show scheduled for 8pm tonight in Kuala Lumpur.
In a Facebook post last night, Anoushka said she was excited to perform in Malaysia again after so many years.
“However, due to circumstances beyond our control, the show has been cancelled by the promoter, Shiraz Projects,” she said.

She also said her team has been assured that all ticket holders will receive full refunds, and advised fans to contact the promoter or their respective point of purchase directly regarding the process.
“I feel terrible for the disappointment and inconvenience this causes our audience, especially those of you who made travel arrangements from further afield.
“Please know how much your support means to me, and how deeply sorry I am that we won't be able to be together as planned tomorrow (Oct 4) night,” she said.
Shiraz Project also shared Anoushka’s statement on its Facebook page, but offered no further explanation.
FMT has reached out to the firm for comment.
Anoushka, who last performed in Malaysia more than a decade ago, was scheduled for a show at the Plenary Hall, Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre tonight.
Netizens have expressed disappointment over the last-minute cancellation, with several asking for an explanation by the promoter.

“Many sitar students and enthusiasts travelled from other cities to be here for the show, having booked hotels, etc. Such last-minute notice without any explanation is just not fair, unless it's an emergency medical reason,” one netizen said.
34311a81d52bb9b1: PETALING JAYA: Cadangan memberi ketua pembangkang peranan menentukan agenda persidangan Dewan Rakyat mendapat reaksi berbeza daripada pemimpin blok kerajaan, dengan Amanah menolaknya manakala seorang Ahli Parlimen PKR mahu perkara itu dipertimbangkan lebih lanjut.

Setiausaha Agung Amanah Faiz Fadzil berkata tiada keperluan melaksanakan cadangan itu ketika ini, manakala Ahli Parlimen Pasir Gudang Hassan Abdul Karim mengalu-alukan langkah berkenaan dan mahu ia dibawa ke Jawatankuasa Pilihan Parlimen.

Faiz berkata walaupun amalan seumpama itu wujud di beberapa negara maju, pendekatan berkenaan tidak sesuai dilaksanakan di Malaysia kerana menurutnya pembangkang masih belum menunjukkan kematangan sebagai semak dan imbang.

“Walaupun ada beberapa negara maju seperti United Kingdom dan Kanada mengamalkan cadangan itu, pembangkang di sana benar-benar matang dalam melaksanakan peranan mereka sebagai semak dan imbang yang berkesan,” katanya kepada FMT.

Beliau memberi contoh tindakan sebahagian Ahli Parlimen pembangkang keluar Dewan ketika perbahasan Suruhanjaya Siasatan Diraja (RCI) berkaitan Tabung Haji, menyebabkan hanya wakil kerajaan dan beberapa Ahli Parlimen pembangkang mengambil bahagian dalam perbahasan.

Faiz turut mempersoalkan pendirian pembangkang dalam menentukan ketua mereka selepas Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar memegang jawatan ketua pembangkang untuk tempoh singkat sebelum Hamzah Zainudin kembali menggalas tugas itu, walaupun PAS merupakan blok terbesar pembangkang.

Menurutnya, pembangkang juga tidak membentangkan bajet alternatif seperti yang lazim dilakukan di beberapa negara maju, sedangkan Pakatan Harapan (PH) pernah berbuat demikian ketika berada dalam pembangkang.

Setiausaha Agung Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) Saifuddin Abdullah pada Jumaat mencadangkan ketua pembangkang diberikan peranan menentukan agenda persidangan Dewan Rakyat sebagai sebahagian usaha memperkukuh amalan perundingan dalam sistem demokrasi.
Ahli Parlimen Indera Mahkota itu berkata pendekatan berkenaan antara pembaharuan yang perlu dipertimbangkan dalam sistem, institusi, kepimpinan dan kerajaan.
Bagaimanapun, Hassan mengambil pendirian berbeza dengan Faiz apabila mengalu-alukan cadangan Saifuddin dan mencadangkan perkara itu dirujuk kepada Jawatankuasa Pilihan Parlimen untuk penelitian.

Beliau berkata sekiranya persetujuan dicapai mengenai bentuk kuasa dan peranan ketua pembangkang dalam menentukan agenda Parlimen, Peraturan Mesyuarat Dewan Rakyat perlu dipinda bagi memberi asas perundangan kepada perubahan itu.

“Jika persetujuan telah dicapai tentang apa bentuk kuasa dan format peranan ketua pembangkang dalam turut sama menentukan agenda Parlimen yang selama ini dikuasai sepenuhnya oleh perdana menteri selaku ketua majlis Dewan Rakyat dan beberapa hal prosedur oleh Yang di-Pertua Dewan Rakyat, maka Peraturan Mesyuarat Dewan Rakyat perlulah dipinda,” katanya.
Hassan berkata perubahan itu boleh memperkukuh proses semak dan imbang serta meningkatkan kebertanggungjawaban kerajaan.

Katanya, langkah itu juga sejajar dengan kedudukan Parlimen yang kini lebih bebas selepas pelaksanaan Akta Perkhidmatan Parlimen, selain dapat memperkukuh prinsip pengasingan kuasa antara badan eksekutif dan legislatif.
a198fb680847722e: PETALING JAYA: The families of the 54 Malaysians still missing after the Nepal floods have called for meetings with Bank Negara Malaysia and the Attorney-General’s Chambers in the next two to three days.

Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (Masfih) said BNM should consider a coordinated mechanism to help the affected families manage their financial commitments while the status of their loved ones remains unresolved.

“The framework could include a moratorium, deferment or temporary restructuring of payments for related financial commitments until the legal status can be determined,” its spokesman, R Manivannan, said.
Manivannan said a centralised mechanism involving the relevant financial institutions would mean families would not have to approach each institution separately.
He said it was important for an AGC representative to attend the meeting with BNM as some financial issues were linked to the legal status of the missing Malaysians.
He also called for the AGC to provide clear guidance on the legal process for obtaining a “presumed death” declaration, including the evidence and documents required and the timeframe involved.
Manivannan said preparations for the legal process could proceed alongside efforts to locate the missing Malaysians and establish their status.
“Hope for a miracle and legal certainty can exist at the same time,” he said.
He called for another 20 DNA samples from a group of 23 missing Malaysians to be sent to Chinese authorities for matching. Three samples from the group have already been submitted.
He said sending the remaining 20 would make samples from all 23 available for comparison and identification.
He also urged Putrajaya to seek China’s assistance in giving the next of kin digital access to a catalogue of personal belongings recovered at Gyirong Port to help identify the items.
Manivannan said the group had previously asked Wisma Putra for information on the catalogue but had yet to receive an update.

Yesterday, BNM said banks were prepared to assist affected families, including through repayment deferments, waivers of fees and charges, and flexibility in documentation requirements pending the completion of legal processes.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Friday that his Nepali counterpart, Balendra Shah, had assured Malaysia of his government’s cooperation in efforts to determine the status of the 54 Malaysians.
Anwar also said he instructed Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar to hold further discussions with the Nepalese authorities.

One of the 55 Malaysians initially reported missing after floods and debris flows struck Nepal on Aug 26 returned to Malaysia on Friday after turning up at the Malaysian embassy in Kathmandu on Thursday.
ec9bb697ba1d1500: BEIJING: Aryna Sabalenka was swatted aside in straight sets by 34th-ranked Nikola Bartunkova in the third round of the China Open on Sunday, leaving the event without its top two seeds.
Czech player Bartunkova, 20, sent down four aces to beat the former world number one 6-4, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes.
"I focused on myself, to be calm," Bartunkova said.
"She's a legend... so I'm really happy that I won the match," she said of the four-time Grand Slam champion.
Bartunkova next faces Austria's Sinja Kraus in the round of 16.
Second-seeded Sabalenka squandered five chances to break serve in the sixth game of the first set, with Bartunkova strong on defence and firing deep.
The 28-year-old from Belarus threw on a cap for the eighth game of the first set as the women switched between playing in the shade and the sun, but it did not turn the tide in her favour.
A frustrated Sabalenka tossed her racquet at a break down in the fourth game of the second set, and lost on the first match point when she returned into the net.
Top seed Elena Rybakina -- who weeks earlier replaced Sabalenka as World No. 1 -- was ousted by Alina Charaeva in the second round on Saturday.
Top seed Alexander Zverev was scheduled to play Novak Djokovic later on Sunday in the quarterfinals of the men's 500-level event also taking place.
The 39-year-old Serbian great enters the match with an extraordinary unbeaten streak in Beijing, but Zverev -- last month's US Open champion -- is in the running for the top men's ranking.
9425aea069e89e73: KYIV: Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv on Sunday, accompanied by CEOs from German defence companies, in a show of support for president Volodymyr Zelensky amid escalating Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities.

Merz will announce a package of measures that includes the release €1 billion in military aid and €350 million for repairs in the energy sector, German government officials said. The visit is also expected to finalise a deal for joint production of various kinds of drones.

"I travelled to Kyiv today because Ukraine needs all our support in the coming weeks," Merz said, saying that Russian forces were bombing towns, residential buildings and heating plants. "If Russia is not stopped, sooner or later its war machine will turn against us."
"I will tell president Zelensky today: 'You can continue to count on our help,'" Merz added.

The German chancellor is accompanied by economic affairs minister Katherina Reiche and an economic delegation including executives from Siemens Energy, Hensoldt, Diehl Defence, Quantum Systems and other firms.
Merz is also expected to press the Ukrainian government for progress on reforms requested by EU partners, including in the fight against corruption.
Zelensky said on Wednesday, after speaking to Merz by phone, that Ukraine would soon finalise the deal with Germany for the production of drones, missiles and related software.

A key focus is expected to be the rapid production of anti-jet drones, which Quantum, a German defence-technology company, has successfully tested. Since the summer, Russia has used dozens of high-speed jet attack drones daily to target civilian and military infrastructure.
In April, Quantum and Ukrainian manufacturer WIY Drones announced the creation of Quantum WIY Industries, a joint venture to produce the Strila interceptor drone and related air-defence technologies.
The deal also involves the joint development and production of weapons with a range of more than 1,000km that Ukraine can use to launch attacks deep inside Russia.

Government officials said the increased cooperation would allow money and technology to flow back to the Federal Republic, where weapons are produced and defences against drones targeting critical infrastructure can be strengthened.
On Thursday, Merz said Germany would not be intimidated by the rising number of hybrid attacks by Russia on European states.

Russia's foreign ministry said in a statement on Saturday that Moscow would continue to systematically hit targets in Ukraine in what it said were retaliatory strikes for Ukrainian attacks on Russia in recent months. It warned foreign nationals and diplomatic staff against staying in or travelling to Ukraine.

Zelensky told Reuters on Saturday his country's armed forces would double down on their attacks on oil refineries in Russia in response to Moscow's "new doctrine" of escalating attacks on civilian infrastructure, which he said was aimed at forcing residents of Kyiv and other cities to flee.

379f3cd7f6467d8c: PETALING JAYA: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has called for an immediate, thorough and transparent investigation after a 16-year-old girl was found dead at a secondary school in Yong Peng, Johor, yesterday afternoon.
Anwar said if there are elements of criminal wrongdoing, firm action must be taken in accordance with the law.
“The safety of our children is a shared responsibility. The government will not compromise on ensuring that their safety and wellbeing are always protected,” he said in a statement.
He also expressed his condolences to the girl’s family and wished them strength and resilience during this difficult time.

Separately, education minister Fadhlina Sidek said she was in Yong Peng this morning to get a firsthand update on the incident from the police, state education department, Batu Pahat education office, and the school.
Based on information from the police, the victim was found unconscious on the school grounds and was subsequently pronounced dead.
“A 16-year-old boy has been arrested and remanded for six days to assist in the investigation.
"The case is being investigated as a murder. The motive and cause of the incident are still under investigation,” she said in a Facebook post.

Fadhlina added that she wanted all matters under the ministry’s purview to be thoroughly examined, including students’ attendance records for extra classes, as well as security measures and patrols at the school.
“The security company (for the school) has also been asked to cooperate with the review.
“If there was any negligence or failure to carry out responsibilities as required, firm action will be taken,” she said.
Fadhlina also wrote that she met with the victim’s family at Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital in Batu Pahat today and stressed that they deserve answers.

The victim, Irene Sofiya Khairoul Faisal, was reportedly found by her grandmother, who went to the school after realising that she had not returned home at about 5.30pm after attending a tuition class.
Separately, Johor police chief Ab Rahaman Arsad in a statement said the victim suffered injuries to her head and several parts of her body.
He also said the suspect, arrested around 7pm yesterday, had no criminal record. Rahaman added that police seized a mobile phone, a set of clothes, and a pair of slippers following the arrest.
d259e9f41464a644: BANGKOK: The US aircraft carrier George H.W. Bush arrived off Thailand's resort island of Phuket on Sunday with about 4,800 personnel aboard for a rest-and-recreation break after months of supporting US operations in the Middle East.
The Nimitz-class carrier had been operating in the Arabian Sea during the conflict with Iran, according to multiple media reports.

The carrier will anchor offshore, while crew members are expected to come ashore through Phuket Deep Sea Port and spend time on the popular southern resort island from October 4 to 9, local media reported.
The visit follows a five-day port call by the US carrier Abraham Lincoln at Laem Chabang in eastern Thailand last month, with about 5,000 sailors and Marines aboard.
A local mayor had estimated each US service member from the Lincoln could spend up to 3,000 baht (US$89) per day during the visit.
Thailand is the United States' only treaty partner in mainland Southeast Asia.
3ff778c787fa39aa: BATU PAHAT: Seorang remaja lelaki berusia 16 tahun direman enam hari, bagi membantu siasatan kes bunuh seorang pelajar perempuan sebaya yang ditemukan tidak sedarkan diri dan berlumuran darah di sebuah sekolah di Yong Peng, semalam.
Ketua Polis Johor Ab Rahaman Arsad berkata suspek ditahan kira-kira 7 malam di sekitar Yong Peng, kira-kira sejam selepas polis menerima maklumat mengenai kejadian berkenaan.
Beliau berkata polis menerima maklumat daripada orang awam pada kira-kira 5.50 petang, selepas mangsa ditemukan dalam keadaan tidak sedarkan diri dan berlumuran darah di sebuah dewan sekolah.
“Mangsa mengalami beberapa kecederaan di bahagian kepala dan badan, sebelum disahkan meninggal dunia di tempat kejadian.
“Proses bedah siasat dijalankan hari ini di Hospital Sultanah Nora Ismail, Batu Pahat,” katanya dalam kenyataan hari ini.
Ab Rahaman berkata suspek ditahan sepasukan anggota Jabatan Siasatan Jenayah Ibu Pejabat Polis Kontinjen Johor bersama dengan Bahagian Siasatan Jenayah Ibu Pejabat Polis Daerah Batu Pahat.
Beliau berkata semakan mendapati remaja berkenaan tidak mempunyai rekod jenayah lampau, manakala sebuah telefon bimbit, sepasang pakaian dan sepasang selipar turut dirampas.
Terdahulu suspek dibawa ke Mahkamah Majistret Batu Pahat bagi proses reman.

Kes disiasat mengikut Seksyen 302 Kanun Keseksaan kerana membunuh, yang memperuntukkan hukuman mati atau penjara minimum 30 tahun dan maksimum 40 tahun serta sebatan tidak kurang 12 kali sekiranya tidak dihukum mati, jika sabit kesalahan.
Ab Rahaman berkata motif serta punca kejadian masih dalam siasatan dan orang ramai diminta tidak membuat spekulasi atau komen yang boleh mengganggu proses siasatan.
Orang ramai yang mempunyai maklumat berkaitan kejadian boleh menghubungi talian Polis Johor menerusi nombor 019-2792095 atau Bilik Gerakan Polis Kontinjen Johor (07-2212999).
93e5585fcf4c4eaf: PETALING JAYA: PAS should be just as bold about its choice of a prime minister candidate now as it was when it previously floated several names, says Bersatu information chief Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz.

Tun Faisal was responding to PAS treasurer Iskandar Abdul Samad’s rejection of calls for the party to state whether it would accept Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi as prime minister if Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional form the next government after the 16th general election.
“Previously, there was no issue of PAS leaders being ‘too early’, ‘afraid’ or ‘shy’ about naming prime minister candidates.
“Strange, isn’t it, that the ‘elephant’ has suddenly become afraid and turned into a ‘mouse’,” he said in a statement.
PAS election director Sanusi Nor previously described the Islamic party as an “elephant” of a party in urging members not to feel inferior to smaller, newly-formed parties.
Tun Faisal said PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang previously said the party’s choice for prime minister was Hamzah Zainudin, the former Bersatu deputy president and now Wawasan president.

He added that the PAS Youth chief in August 2025 had openly named five potential prime ministers: Hadi, PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man, vice-presidents Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar and Idris Ahmad, and Hamzah.
In September 2025, the wing at its muktamar named Tuan Ibrahim as its candidate for the prime minister’s post under PN, before switching to Samsuri in February after he took over as PN chairman.

Tun Faisal said Iskandar should simply explain that Samsuri or any other PAS leader cannot be PAS’s prime minister candidate because, so far, the Islamic party does not appear to have a candidate with the necessary experience and ability.
“After all, the PAS president himself has not named a PAS leader as his candidate, but instead named a leader from another party,” he said.

Iskandar yesterday said the question was premature and had not been discussed by the party. He also described the prediction by former DAP leader Ong Kian Ming, who is now a political analyst, that BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamidi would be the next prime minister, as mere speculation.
As such, he said there was no need to entertain Amanah vice-president Mahfuz Omar’s call for PAS to address the issue based on Ong’s prediction.

05dc312e134aff1f: I can’t add much to the paeans to the late Dr Hasmah Ali from the many who knew her better. But I’d like to say a few things that reflect on the beauty of her long marriage to the indomitable ex-prime minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad, who is even older and currently also in poor health.

Mahathir never hid her. She was always at his side on every occasion that protocol and decorum allowed. Mahathir, one of the toughest of all men and one of the hardest of all politicians, always looked happy beside her, both often smiling that enigmatic smile that seemed to say, "we’re equals here".

The sight of a heartbroken Mahathir at her funeral was heartbreaking in itself. Even his harshest critic or political enemy could feel and empathise with his pain and loss. AlFatihah, and may I add my own condolences to her family and those who love and respect her, and may she rest in peace.

Her passing reminds me of my own parents, both of whom passed away many years ago. My parents, in the tradition of many devout Muslims, talked about death often and matter-of-factly, not in any sombre or ghoulish way, but just death as the inevitable next act that they, and soon enough all human beings, must face.

Going to meet her Maker held no fear for my mother. But she did say openly to all and perhaps even to my father himself that she wished he would pass on before her for a very simple, practical reason – that without her he would find life hard and lonely and difficult to bear, even with his children and grandchildren beside him.

Now, my father was the tough, hard man in the family. He had been a fisherman, a farmer, a shopkeeper, often a street hawker and if his tales are to be believed, also a soldier employed by the British to defend Penang against the Japanese invasion in late 1941, armed with an old rifle and two bullets.

He had a temper, too, one well known across my village. You didn’t mess with Pak ‘Ain, as my father was known. His fuse, once lit, could not be put out but would run its course no matter how much damage it did to people and things.
But my mother matched, even surpassed, the sacrifices my father made to bring up our family amidst poverty, and in my father’s case, frequent ill health.

What she said about death was not because she wished for a great last few years unburdened by matrimonial duties, but was just an expression of her care and concern for her husband, who would truly be lost without her.
She didn’t say it wishing to unburden herself of an increasingly frail man and it left unsaid her own strength and self-sacrifice that had held the family together through 55 years of marriage.

And that’s how things turned out. She passed away in 2000, three years after my father. I always knew how her strength, unspoken and unsung as it was, had helped our family survive our own slings and arrows of outrageous fortune and helped make us who we are today.

I suspect Hasmah was made of the same stern stuff as my mother, and many other mothers out there. She helped Mahathir withstand the pressures of politics while raising their family, all the while smiling serenely as if she didn’t have a care in the world.
I can only imagine Mahathir's heartbreak at losing his life partner so late in life.
Malaysians have had both Tuns in our lives for so long that we perhaps have taken their existence for granted.
I pray for strength for Mahathir during these sad times. Even the hardest and toughest of humans still needs a strong, steady partner to weather the vicissitudes of life.
Nothing is forever. Hasmah has gone to meet her Maker, and may He shower her with the rewards of having led a good life. May He also give Mahathir all the strength he needs to carry on.
